== ConLeche/Denotes.lean#L248-L268
   248  structure Model (V : Type w) [SetTheory V] (env : Env) where
   249    /-- the set a constant denotes, per level assignment -/
   250    cval : Name → (LevelParam → Nat) → V
   251    /-- every stored constant is a member of what its type denotes, at
   252    every level assignment (and every variable environment — the type
   253    is closed) -/
   254    mem : ∀ c ∈ env.consts, ∀ (φ : LevelParam → Nat) (ρ : BVarIdx → V),
   255      ∃ T, Denotes cval env φ ρ c.toConstantVal.type T ∧ cval c.name φ ∈ˢ T
   256    /-- whatever the built-in `False` denotes is the empty set -/
   257    false_empty : ∀ (φ : LevelParam → Nat) (ρ : BVarIdx → V) (F : V),
   258      Denotes cval env φ ρ (.const falseName []) F → F = empty
   259    /-- whatever the built-in `Eq` denotes is set equality: at a type `A`
   260    of the universe the level `u` names, and two of its members `a` and
   261    `b`, `@Eq.{u} A a b` denotes the truth value of `a = b`.  The three
   262    membership premises are the graph's domains — `Eq`'s denotation is a
   263    three-fold graph over `univ (Level.eval φ u)`, then over `A`, then
   264    over `A` again, and a graph read off its domain says nothing -/
   265    eq_equality : ∀ (u : Level) (φ : LevelParam → Nat) (ρ : BVarIdx → V) (E A a b : V),
   266      Denotes cval env φ ρ (.const eqName [u]) E →
   267      A ∈ˢ univ (Level.eval φ u) → a ∈ˢ A → b ∈ˢ A →
   268      app (app (app E A) a) b = eqv a b

== ConLeche/SetTheory/Core.lean#L95-L100
    95  /-- A model of set theory of exactly the strength the checker needs:
    96  membership, the six ZF⁻ axioms (extensionality, pairing, union, power
    97  set, regularity, Lean-level replacement), and an ω-chain of
    98  Grothendieck universes.  Infinity is derivable; choice is inherited
    99  from the meta-logic (`Classical.choice`); see the module docstring. -/
   100  class SetTheory (V : Type u) where

== whitepaper/Fragment/Interp.lean#L139-L146
   139  noncomputable def interp (M : Name → List Nat → V) (φ : Name → Nat) : (Nat → V) → Expr → V
   140    | ρ, .bvar i => ρ i
   141    | _, .sort u => typeU (u.eval φ)
   142    | _, .const c ls => M c (ls.map (Level.eval φ))
   143    | ρ, .app f a => app (interp M φ ρ f) (interp M φ ρ a)
   144    | ρ, .lam A b => lamV (interp M φ ρ A) fun x => interp M φ (cons x ρ) b
   145    | ρ, .pi A B => piV (interp M φ ρ A) fun x => interp M φ (cons x ρ) B
   146    | ρ, .letE _ v b => interp M φ (cons (interp M φ ρ v) ρ) b

== whitepaper/Fragment/WellDenoted.lean#L58-L78
    58  def WellDenoted : (Nat → V) → Expr → Prop
    59    | _, .bvar _ => True
    60    | _, .sort _ => True
    61    | _, .const _ _ => True
    62    | ρ, .app f a =>
    63      WellDenoted ρ f ∧ WellDenoted ρ a ∧
    64        ∃ (p : Bool) (A : V) (B : V → V),
    65          interp M φ ρ f ∈ˢ piR p A B ∧ interp M φ ρ a ∈ˢ A ∧
    66          (p = true → ∀ x, x ∈ˢ A → B x ∈ˢ univ 0) ∧ (p = false → IsTy A)
    67    | ρ, .lam A b =>
    68      WellDenoted ρ A ∧ IsTy (interp M φ ρ A) ∧
    69        (∀ x, x ∈ˢ interp M φ ρ A → WellDenoted (cons x ρ) b) ∧
    70        ∃ B : V → V,
    71          (∀ x, x ∈ˢ interp M φ ρ A → interp M φ (cons x ρ) b ∈ˢ B x) ∧
    72          (∀ x, x ∈ˢ interp M φ ρ A → IsTy (B x))
    73    | ρ, .pi A B =>
    74      WellDenoted ρ A ∧ IsTy (interp M φ ρ A) ∧
    75        (∀ x, x ∈ˢ interp M φ ρ A → WellDenoted (cons x ρ) B) ∧
    76        (∀ x, x ∈ˢ interp M φ ρ A → IsTy (interp M φ (cons x ρ) B))
    77    | ρ, .letE _ v b =>
    78      WellDenoted ρ v ∧ WellDenoted (cons (interp M φ ρ v) ρ) b

== whitepaper/Fragment/Lib.lean#L477-L481
   477  /-- **The function space, regime read off the fibres.** -/
   478  noncomputable def piV (A : V) (B : V → V) : V := piR (propB A B) A B
   479  
   480  /-- **The abstraction, regime read off the body values.** -/
   481  noncomputable def lamV (A : V) (F : V → V) : V := lamR (ptB A F) A F

== whitepaper/Fragment/Syntax.lean#L29-L48
    29  /-- Terms. -/
    30  inductive Expr where
    31    /-- A bound variable, by de Bruijn index. -/
    32    | bvar (i : Nat)
    33    /-- The sort `Sort l`. -/
    34    | sort (l : Level)
    35    /-- A constant of the environment at a level instantiation. -/
    36    | const (c : Name) (ls : List Level)
    37    /-- Application. -/
    38    | app (f a : Expr)
    39    /-- Abstraction `fun (x : A) => b`. -/
    40    | lam (A b : Expr)
    41    /-- The Π-type `(x : A) → B`. -/
    42    | pi (A B : Expr)
    43    /-- `let x : ty := v; b`.  Kept as Lean stores it: the
    44    checker substitutes the value (`Red.zeta`, `Infer.letE`), and the
    45    interpretation reads the body at the value's value, ignoring the type
    46    (`Interp.lean`), as con-leche's `Denotes` `let` rule does. -/
    47    | letE (ty v b : Expr)
    48    deriving DecidableEq

== whitepaper/Fragment/Syntax.lean#L65-L75
    65  /-- Instantiate the bound variable `k` by `a` (and lower the indices
    66  above it): `e.inst a` is `e[x := a]` for the innermost binder. -/
    67  def inst : Expr → Expr → (k : Nat := 0) → Expr
    68    | bvar i, a, k =>
    69      if i < k then bvar i else if i = k then liftN k a else bvar (i - 1)
    70    | sort u, _, _ => sort u
    71    | const c ls, _, _ => const c ls
    72    | app f b, a, k => app (inst f a k) (inst b a k)
    73    | lam A b, a, k => lam (inst A a k) (inst b a (k + 1))
    74    | pi A B, a, k => pi (inst A a k) (inst B a (k + 1))
    75    | letE T v b, a, k => letE (inst T a k) (inst v a k) (inst b a (k + 1))

== whitepaper/Fragment/Level.lean#L29-L43
    29  /-- Universe levels (`Lean.Level` without `mvar`). -/
    30  inductive Level where
    31    /-- `Prop`'s level, `0`. -/
    32    | zero
    33    /-- The successor level `u + 1`. -/
    34    | succ (l : Level)
    35    /-- The maximum `max u v`. -/
    36    | max (a b : Level)
    37    /-- The impredicative maximum: `imax u v` is `0` when `v` is `0`,
    38    else `max u v` — so a `∀` whose codomain is a proposition is a
    39    proposition whatever its domain's level. -/
    40    | imax (a b : Level)
    41    /-- A level parameter of the enclosing declaration. -/
    42    | param (n : Name)
    43    deriving DecidableEq, Repr

== ConLeche/Kernel/Expr.lean#L39-L44
    39  inductive Level where
    40    | zero
    41    | succ (u : Level)
    42    | max (u v : Level)
    43    | imax (u v : Level)
    44    | param (n : Name)

== whitepaper/Fragment/Level.lean#L50-L56
    50  /-- The value of a level under a *valuation* `φ` of its parameters. -/
    51  def eval (φ : Name → Nat) : Level → Nat
    52    | zero => 0
    53    | succ l => eval φ l + 1
    54    | max a b => Max.max (eval φ a) (eval φ b)
    55    | imax a b => imaxNat (eval φ a) (eval φ b)
    56    | param n => φ n

== ConLeche/Verify/Level.lean#L26-L31
    26  @[expose] def eval (φ : Name → Nat) : Level → Nat
    27    | .zero => 0
    28    | .succ l => eval φ l + 1
    29    | .max l r => Max.max (eval φ l) (eval φ r)
    30    | .imax l r => if eval φ r = 0 then 0 else Max.max (eval φ l) (eval φ r)
    31    | .param n => φ n

== whitepaper/Fragment/Level.lean#L130-L145
   130  /-- **The level oracle** — the checker's decision procedures for `≤` and
   131  `=` on levels, assumed sound and complete with respect to `eval`: a
   132  parameter of the development, never defined here.  (`le` is what the
   133  inductive installs of the environment section consume; the env-free
   134  fragment uses `eq` alone.) -/
   135  class LevelOracle where
   136    /-- `le u v = true` decides `u ≤ v` at every valuation. -/
   137    le : Level → Level → Bool
   138    /-- `eq u v = true` decides `u = v` at every valuation. -/
   139    eq : Level → Level → Bool
   140    /-- Soundness and completeness of `le`. -/
   141    le_iff : ∀ a b : Level, le a b = true ↔ ∀ φ : Name → Nat, Level.eval φ a ≤ Level.eval φ b
   142    /-- Soundness and completeness of `eq`. -/
   143    eq_iff : ∀ a b : Level, eq a b = true ↔ ∀ φ : Name → Nat, Level.eval φ a = Level.eval φ b
   144  
   145  namespace Level

== ConLeche/Kernel/Level.lean#L144-L146
   144  /-- Decide `l ≤ r` semantically; `none` is an exhausted comparison. -/
   145  def leq (l r : Level) : Option Bool :=
   146    leqCore defaultFuel (simplify l) (simplify r) 0

== ConLeche/Kernel/Level.lean#L164-L167
   164  def isEquiv (l r : Level) : Option Bool := do
   165    if l == r then pure true
   166    else if simplify l = simplify r then pure true
   167    else if ← leq l r then leq r l else pure false

== ConLeche/Verify/Level.lean#L173-L174
   173  theorem leq_sound {l r : Level} (h : leq l r = some true) :
   174      ∀ φ, eval φ l ≤ eval φ r := by

== ConLeche/Verify/Level.lean#L201-L202
   201  theorem isEquiv_sound {l r : Level} (h : isEquiv l r = some true) :
   202      ∀ φ, eval φ l = eval φ r := by

== whitepaper/Fragment/Rules.lean#L56-L798
    56  mutual
    57  
    58  /-- **Reduction**: the head steps of the checker's `whnf`, chained. -/
    59  inductive Red (env : Env) : List Expr → Expr → Expr → Prop where
    60    /-- No step (`Red.refl`, `Rel.lean:106`). -/
    61    | refl {Γ : List Expr} {e : Expr} : Red env Γ e e
    62    /-- Chaining (`Red.trans`, `Rel.lean:111`).  A reduction is a
    63    denotation identity, so chaining costs nothing semantically. -/
    64    | trans {Γ : List Expr} {e₁ e₂ e₃ : Expr} :
    65        Red env Γ e₁ e₂ → Red env Γ e₂ e₃ → Red env Γ e₁ e₃
    66    /-- Head reduction inside an application (`Red.appFn`,
    67    `Rel.lean:116`): the head is reduced before a redex is looked for. -/
    68    | appFn {Γ : List Expr} {f f' a : Expr} :
    69        Red env Γ f f' → Red env Γ (app f a) (app f' a)
    70    /-- **β**: at every binder, with **no premise** — no
    71    inference of the argument, no comparison with the binder's domain.
    72    This is Lean's own β (`whnf_core`).  The model needs no premise
    73    (`Sound.lean`, `Red.beta_sound`): a reduction claims nothing of a
    74    redex that denotes the point, and a redex that does not has a lambda that
    75    does not, so a graph, which determines its domain: the argument lies
    76    in the lambda's domain because it lies in the domain of the slot the
    77    semantic invariant gives the application.
    78    -/
    79    | beta {Γ : List Expr} {A b a : Expr} :
    80        Red env Γ (app (lam A b) a) (b.inst a)
    81    /-- **ζ**: a `let` reduces to its body with the value
    82    substituted, with no certificate, as β (con-leche's `whnfCore` on
    83    `.letE`, S0's `inst1M b v`; official `whnf_core`).  Unlike β it
    84    needs no case split on the point: the `let` and its reduct denote
    85    alike at every environment (`interp_zeta`). -/
    86    | zeta {Γ : List Expr} {T v b : Expr} :
    87        Red env Γ (letE T v b) (b.inst v)
    88    /-- **δ** (`Red.delta`, `Rel.lean:140`): a definition unfolds to its
    89    value, at the use's level instantiation.  (With `appFn`, an applied
    90    definition unfolds at its head.) -/
    91    | delta {Γ : List Expr} {c : Name} {ls : List Level} {ci : ConstInfo} {v : Expr} :
    92        env.find? c = some ci → ci.value? = some v →
    93        ls.length = ci.lparams.length →
    94        Red env Γ (const c ls) (v.instL ci.lparams ls)
    95    /-- **ι** (`Red.iota`, `Rel.lean:200`): a stored recursor applied to
    96    exactly its telescope — `numParams` parameters, `numMotives` motives,
    97    `numMinors` minor premises, `numIndices` indices and the major
    98    premise — whose major reduces to a constructor application with a
    99    rule, fires the rule: the rule's right-hand side, at the use's
   100    levels, applied to the parameters, motives and minors, then to the
   101    constructor's fields (its arguments after the parameters).  The rule
   102    is one of the block's own constructors' (no stored instantiation,
   103    `RecRule.inst`); an auxiliary recursor's rule fires by
   104    `Red.iotaNested`.
   105  
   106    The **certificates** are the fragment's form of `Rel.lean`'s `CertsF`
   107    and `piResidual` premises (`:227-236`).  The recursor's spine before the
   108    major needs none: a reduction claims nothing of a redex that is the
   109    point, and a redex that is not the point fits the recursor's telescope
   110    by the invariant's application slots (`teleFit_of_ne_pt`).  The reduced
   111    major's slot is certified — its type inferred and found definitionally
   112    equal to the domain the recursor's telescope leaves after the spine
   113    (`Expr.piResidual`) — and so is the constructor's argument spine against
   114    its stored type's `Π`-telescope (`Expr.piDomains`; the stored types have
   115    the spine's length of syntactic binders, `Expr.hasPis`).  Both are
   116    needed only where the major may denote the point (a family that may be a
   117    proposition): where the major's domain is strict, `iota_core_strict`
   118    (`Sound.lean`) needs neither; where the constructor's family is a
   119    proposition at every valuation, `Red.iotaProp` needs no slot
   120    certificate.  They make the environment's ι law (`EnvModel.lean`,
   121    `RecRuleLaw`) applicable: they put every argument in its domain.
   122  
   123    The **three comparisons** after them are `Rel.lean`'s too (`:213-241`,
   124    there in the certified case only): the constructor's levels are the
   125    recursor's (its last `usj.length` ones — a large eliminator carries
   126    one extra level in front), the constructor's parameters are
   127    definitionally the recursor's, and the constructor's residual type
   128    (`Expr.piResidual`: the family at the constructor's own parameters and
   129    index expressions, with the fields substituted in) has index
   130    expressions definitionally equal to the recursor's index arguments. In
   131    the model they matter exactly when the family is a proposition: there
   132    the major denotes the one point, the certificates say only that the
   133    fibre is inhabited, and the fields the rule's right-hand side receives
   134    can be related to the recursor's own parameters and indices through
   135    these comparisons alone (`Install.lean`). -/
   136    | iota {Γ : List Expr} {c : Name} {us : List Level} {ci : ConstInfo}
   137        {numParams numMotives numMinors numIndices : Nat} {rules : List RecRule}
   138        {args : List Expr} {major : Expr} {cj : Name} {usj : List Level}
   139        {cij : ConstInfo} {margs : List Expr} {rl : RecRule}
   140        {dM bM tM : Expr} {doms' tys' : List Expr}
   141        {residual : Expr} {I : Name} {lsI : List Level} {rps ridx : List Expr} :
   142        env.find? c = some ci →
   143        ci.kind = .recursor numParams numMotives numMinors numIndices rules →
   144        us.length = ci.lparams.length →
   145        args.length = numParams + numMotives + numMinors + numIndices + 1 →
   146        ci.type.hasPis (numParams + numMotives + numMinors + numIndices + 1) = true →
   147        Red env Γ (args.getD (numParams + numMotives + numMinors + numIndices) (bvar 0))
   148          major →
   149        major = mkAppN (const cj usj) margs →
   150        rl ∈ rules → rl.ctor = cj → rl.inst = none →
   151        env.find? cj = some cij →
   152        usj.length = cij.lparams.length →
   153        margs.length = numParams + rl.nfields →
   154        cij.type.hasPis (numParams + rl.nfields) = true →
   155        -- the major's slot certificate (the recursor's spine before it needs none)
   156        piResidual (ci.type.instL ci.lparams us)
   157          (args.take (numParams + numMotives + numMinors + numIndices)) = some (pi dM bM) →
   158        Infer env Γ major tM → DefEq env Γ tM dM →
   159        -- the constructor's telescope certificate
   160        piDomains (cij.type.instL cij.lparams usj) margs = some doms' →
   161        tys'.length = doms'.length →
   162        (∀ p ∈ margs.zip tys', Infer env Γ p.1 p.2) →
   163        (∀ p ∈ tys'.zip doms', DefEq env Γ p.1 p.2) →
   164        -- the constructor's levels, parameters and residual indices against the recursor's
   165        Level.eqList usj (us.drop (us.length - usj.length)) = true →
   166        (∀ p ∈ (margs.take numParams).zip (args.take numParams), DefEq env Γ p.1 p.2) →
   167        piResidual (cij.type.instL cij.lparams usj) margs = some residual →
   168        residual = mkAppN (const I lsI) (rps ++ ridx) →
   169        rps.length = numParams →
   170        (∀ p ∈ ridx.zip ((args.take (numParams + numMotives + numMinors + numIndices)).drop
   171          (numParams + numMotives + numMinors)), DefEq env Γ p.1 p.2) →
   172        Red env Γ (mkAppN (const c us) args)
   173          (mkAppN (rl.rhs.instL ci.lparams us)
   174            (args.take (numParams + numMotives + numMinors) ++ margs.drop numParams))
   175    /-- **ι on a family in `Prop`, with no major-slot certificate**
   176    (the checker's certified case of ι).  `Red.iota` without the reduced
   177    major's slot certificate, for a constructor whose family's sort
   178    evaluates to zero at every valuation: the family `I` the
   179    constructor's residual type is headed by is stored, its type walked
   180    along the residual's parameters and indices leaves `Sort u`, and the
   181    oracle decides `u = 0`.  The constructor's telescope certificate stays
   182    at the full grade (every parameter and field), and so do the
   183    three comparisons.  Why the slot needs nothing: the unreduced major
   184    lies in the slot whenever the redex is not the point, and where it is
   185    the point so is the reduced constructor application
   186    (`ctorApp_eq_pt_of_sortZero`, `Red.iota_core_prop`).  This covers the
   187    families that are always propositions (`Acc`); a family that may be
   188    a proposition at some valuations only (`Quot.{u}`, `PUnit.{u}`) also
   189    goes by `Red.iotaSlot`, which reads the environment's fibre law at the
   190    others. -/
   191    | iotaProp {Γ : List Expr} {c : Name} {us : List Level} {ci : ConstInfo}
   192        {numParams numMotives numMinors numIndices : Nat} {rules : List RecRule}
   193        {args : List Expr} {major : Expr} {cj : Name} {usj : List Level}
   194        {cij : ConstInfo} {margs : List Expr} {rl : RecRule}
   195        {dM bM : Expr} {doms' tys' : List Expr}
   196        {residual : Expr} {I : Name} {lsI : List Level} {rps ridx : List Expr}
   197        {Ii : ConstInfo} {u : Level} :
   198        env.find? c = some ci →
   199        ci.kind = .recursor numParams numMotives numMinors numIndices rules →
   200        us.length = ci.lparams.length →
   201        args.length = numParams + numMotives + numMinors + numIndices + 1 →
   202        ci.type.hasPis (numParams + numMotives + numMinors + numIndices + 1) = true →
   203        Red env Γ (args.getD (numParams + numMotives + numMinors + numIndices) (bvar 0))
   204          major →
   205        major = mkAppN (const cj usj) margs →
   206        rl ∈ rules → rl.ctor = cj → rl.inst = none →
   207        env.find? cj = some cij →
   208        usj.length = cij.lparams.length →
   209        margs.length = numParams + rl.nfields →
   210        cij.type.hasPis (numParams + rl.nfields) = true →
   211        -- the major's slot, located but not certified
   212        piResidual (ci.type.instL ci.lparams us)
   213          (args.take (numParams + numMotives + numMinors + numIndices)) = some (pi dM bM) →
   214        -- the constructor's telescope certificate
   215        piDomains (cij.type.instL cij.lparams usj) margs = some doms' →
   216        tys'.length = doms'.length →
   217        (∀ p ∈ margs.zip tys', Infer env Γ p.1 p.2) →
   218        (∀ p ∈ tys'.zip doms', DefEq env Γ p.1 p.2) →
   219        -- the constructor's levels, parameters and residual indices against the recursor's
   220        Level.eqList usj (us.drop (us.length - usj.length)) = true →
   221        (∀ p ∈ (margs.take numParams).zip (args.take numParams), DefEq env Γ p.1 p.2) →
   222        piResidual (cij.type.instL cij.lparams usj) margs = some residual →
   223        residual = mkAppN (const I lsI) (rps ++ ridx) →
   224        rps.length = numParams →
   225        (∀ p ∈ ridx.zip ((args.take (numParams + numMotives + numMinors + numIndices)).drop
   226          (numParams + numMotives + numMinors)), DefEq env Γ p.1 p.2) →
   227        -- the constructor's family is a proposition at every valuation
   228        env.find? I = some Ii →
   229        lsI.length = Ii.lparams.length →
   230        Ii.type.hasPis (rps ++ ridx).length = true →
   231        piResidual (Ii.type.instL Ii.lparams lsI) (rps ++ ridx) = some (sort u) →
   232        LevelOracle.eq u .zero = true →
   233        Red env Γ (mkAppN (const c us) args)
   234          (mkAppN (rl.rhs.instL ci.lparams us)
   235            (args.take (numParams + numMotives + numMinors) ++ margs.drop numParams))
   236    /-- **ι, nested** (con-leche's `.nested`-certified rules, task #48):
   237    a rule of an auxiliary recursor fires on a constructor of the
   238    block's *container*, whose parameters are not the recursor's.  The
   239    rule stores the constructor's expected levels (over the recursor's
   240    level parameters) and expected parameters (terms under the
   241    recursor's parameter binders, `RecRule.inst`); the three
   242    comparisons of `Red.iota` become: the constructor's levels are the
   243    stored ones at the use's levels, its parameters are definitionally
   244    the stored ones at the recursor's parameter arguments
   245    (`Expr.instChain`), and the residual's index expressions are
   246    definitionally the recursor's index arguments.  The constructor's
   247    own parameter count comes from its record.  The telescope
   248    certificates are as in `Red.iota`. -/
   249    | iotaNested {Γ : List Expr} {c : Name} {us : List Level} {ci : ConstInfo}
   250        {numParams numMotives numMinors numIndices : Nat} {rules : List RecRule}
   251        {args : List Expr} {major : Expr} {cj : Name} {usj : List Level}
   252        {cij : ConstInfo} {I' : Name} {nPc nfj : Nat} {margs : List Expr} {rl : RecRule}
   253        {lvs : List Level} {pinst : List Expr}
   254        {dM bM tM : Expr} {doms' tys' : List Expr}
   255        {residual : Expr} {I : Name} {lsI : List Level} {rps ridx : List Expr} :
   256        env.find? c = some ci →
   257        ci.kind = .recursor numParams numMotives numMinors numIndices rules →
   258        us.length = ci.lparams.length →
   259        args.length = numParams + numMotives + numMinors + numIndices + 1 →
   260        ci.type.hasPis (numParams + numMotives + numMinors + numIndices + 1) = true →
   261        Red env Γ (args.getD (numParams + numMotives + numMinors + numIndices) (bvar 0))
   262          major →
   263        major = mkAppN (const cj usj) margs →
   264        rl ∈ rules → rl.ctor = cj → rl.inst = some (lvs, pinst) →
   265        env.find? cj = some cij →
   266        cij.kind = .ctor I' nPc nfj →
   267        usj.length = cij.lparams.length →
   268        margs.length = nPc + rl.nfields →
   269        cij.type.hasPis (nPc + rl.nfields) = true →
   270        piResidual (ci.type.instL ci.lparams us)
   271          (args.take (numParams + numMotives + numMinors + numIndices)) = some (pi dM bM) →
   272        Infer env Γ major tM → DefEq env Γ tM dM →
   273        piDomains (cij.type.instL cij.lparams usj) margs = some doms' →
   274        tys'.length = doms'.length →
   275        (∀ p ∈ margs.zip tys', Infer env Γ p.1 p.2) →
   276        (∀ p ∈ tys'.zip doms', DefEq env Γ p.1 p.2) →
   277        -- the constructor's levels and parameters against the stored instantiation
   278        Level.eqList usj (lvs.map (Level.subst ci.lparams us)) = true →
   279        pinst.length = nPc →
   280        (∀ p ∈ (margs.take nPc).zip
   281          (pinst.map fun e => instChain (e.instL ci.lparams us) (args.take numParams)),
   282          DefEq env Γ p.1 p.2) →
   283        piResidual (cij.type.instL cij.lparams usj) margs = some residual →
   284        residual = mkAppN (const I lsI) (rps ++ ridx) →
   285        rps.length = nPc →
   286        (∀ p ∈ ridx.zip ((args.take (numParams + numMotives + numMinors + numIndices)).drop
   287          (numParams + numMotives + numMinors)), DefEq env Γ p.1 p.2) →
   288        Red env Γ (mkAppN (const c us) args)
   289          (mkAppN (rl.rhs.instL ci.lparams us)
   290            (args.take (numParams + numMotives + numMinors) ++ margs.drop nPc))
   291  
   292    /-- **ι with no major-slot certificate and no level test** (the
   293    checker's certified case of ι).  `Red.iota`
   294    without the reduced major's slot certificate, for any family: the
   295    constructor's telescope certificate stays at the full grade (every
   296    parameter and field), and so do the three comparisons; nothing
   297    else is tested.  Why the slot needs nothing: where the unreduced
   298    major is not the point its reduction claim gives the reduct; where it
   299    is, the environment's slot law (`EnvModel.rec_rules_slot`) makes
   300    the constructor application the point too, given the redex is not
   301    (`Sound.lean`, `slot_of_law`, `iota_core_slot`).  On the generated
   302    recursors that law holds because the major's domain is the
   303    constructor's own family at the recursor's levels, a fibre holding the
   304    point is a truth value there, and the constructor of a family in
   305    `Prop` is the point (`IndSpec.rec_rule_slot`).  No premise links the
   306    major's domain to the constructor's family: the installation proves
   307    the slot law of every generated rule (`InstallIota.lean`).  This
   308    is the rule for a family that is a proposition at some valuations
   309    only (`Quot.{u}`, `PUnit.{u}`). -/
   310    | iotaSlot {Γ : List Expr} {c : Name} {us : List Level} {ci : ConstInfo}

   315        {residual : Expr} {I : Name} {lsI : List Level} {rps ridx : List Expr} :
   316        env.find? c = some ci →
   317        ci.kind = .recursor numParams numMotives numMinors numIndices rules →
   318        us.length = ci.lparams.length →

   320        ci.type.hasPis (numParams + numMotives + numMinors + numIndices + 1) = true →
   321        Red env Γ (args.getD (numParams + numMotives + numMinors + numIndices) (bvar 0))
   322          major →

   324        rl ∈ rules → rl.ctor = cj → rl.inst = none →
   325        env.find? cj = some cij →
   326        usj.length = cij.lparams.length →

   329        -- the major's slot, located but not certified

   394    /-- **ι, case 2** (the checker's ι case test): `Red.iota`

   427        -- case 2: the major's domain is a stored family whose sort is never `Prop` at the use

   493    /-- **ι by K** (Lean's
   494    `to_cnstr_when_K`): a recursor whose rule is flagged K
   495    (`RecRule.k`: one family, always a proposition, one constructor
   496    with no fields — `Eq`, `HEq`, `True`) reduces on its major **as it
   497    stands**, with no constructor in sight, to the rule's right-hand
   498    side at the recursor's parameters, motives and minors.  There is no
   499    certificate, no level, parameter or index comparison, and the major
   500    is not reduced.  What stays is K's **type check**, as in Lean: the
   501    major's inferred type reduces to a family application
   502    `I.{lsI} targs`, the constructor fabricated at its parameters
   503    `rl.ctor.{lsI} (targs.take numParams)` has a type `tF`, and
   504    `tF ≡ I.{lsI} targs`.  That check decides whether the step is taken
   505    (a verdict test); no claim consumes it.  Soundness is the
   506    environment's K law (`EnvModel.rec_rules_k`, proved in the
   507    installer by inversion of the least fixed point) with
   508    `Red.iotaK_core_sem`: a redex that is not the point fits the
   509    recursor's telescope, the major included, and the law needs nothing
   510    more. -/
   511    | iotaK {Γ : List Expr} {c : Name} {us : List Level} {ci : ConstInfo}
   512        {numParams numMotives numMinors numIndices : Nat} {rules : List RecRule}
   513        {args : List Expr} {rl : RecRule} {tM : Expr} {I : Name} {lsI : List Level}
   514        {targs : List Expr} {tF : Expr} :
   515        env.find? c = some ci →
   516        ci.kind = .recursor numParams numMotives numMinors numIndices rules →
   517        us.length = ci.lparams.length →
   518        args.length = numParams + numMotives + numMinors + numIndices + 1 →
   519        ci.type.hasPis (numParams + numMotives + numMinors + numIndices + 1) = true →
   520        rl ∈ rules → rl.k = true →
   521        -- K's type check on the major as it stands (a verdict test, consumed by no claim)
   522        Infer env Γ (args.getD (numParams + numMotives + numMinors + numIndices) (bvar 0)) tM →
   523        Red env Γ tM (mkAppN (const I lsI) targs) →
   524        Infer env Γ (mkAppN (const rl.ctor lsI) (targs.take numParams)) tF →
   525        DefEq env Γ tF (mkAppN (const I lsI) targs) →
   526        Red env Γ (mkAppN (const c us) args)
   527          (mkAppN (rl.rhs.instL ci.lparams us) (args.take (numParams + numMotives + numMinors)))
   528  
   529  /-- **Definitional equality**: the verdict `true` of the checker's
   530  `isDefEq`.
   531  
   532  **There is no `trans` rule, deliberately** (`Rel.lean:334-357`).
   533  The relation is the checker's verdict on two terms that are
   534  well-formed *together*, a fact no rule states because well-formedness
   535  is semantic (`WellDenoted`) and may not enter this inductive.  Every
   536  rule respects one discipline instead: **the subject of each `DefEq`
   537  premise is a subterm of the conclusion or is produced by a `Red` or
   538  `Infer` premise** (a reduct, an inferred type), so the soundness proof
   539  always has the premise's terms — and their invariant — in hand.  A
   540  `trans` rule is the unique rule that would break it: its middle term
   541  comes from nowhere, so nothing supplies its invariant, and the
   542  induction has nothing to apply the hypothesis to.  Nor does the
   543  checker chain through an arbitrary middle term: every comparison it
   544  makes is one of the rules below, and its one way to chain is
   545  "reduce, then continue": `redL`.
   546  -/
   547  inductive DefEq (env : Env) : List Expr → Expr → Expr → Prop where
   548    /-- The syntactic fast path (`DefEq.refl`, `Rel.lean:362`). -/
   549    | refl {Γ : List Expr} {a : Expr} : DefEq env Γ a a
   550    /-- Symmetry (`DefEq.symm`, `Rel.lean:365`).  Not a checker move: the
   551    constructor from which every right-hand variant of a one-sided rule
   552    is derived. -/
   553    | symm {Γ : List Expr} {a b : Expr} : DefEq env Γ a b → DefEq env Γ b a
   554    /-- **Reduce the left side, then continue** (`DefEq.redL`,
   555    `Rel.lean:370`): the recursive structure of `isDefEq` — head
   556    normalisation of either side (with `symm`) and every lazy-δ
   557    continuation. -/
   558    | redL {Γ : List Expr} {a a' b : Expr} :
   559        Red env Γ a a' → DefEq env Γ a' b → DefEq env Γ a b
   560    /-- Two sorts, by the level oracle (`DefEq.sort`, `Rel.lean:373`). -/
   561    | sort {Γ : List Expr} {u v : Level} :
   562        LevelOracle.eq u v = true → DefEq env Γ (sort u) (sort v)
   563    /-- Two constants of the same name at oracle-equal levels
   564    (`DefEq.const`, `Rel.lean:384`). -/
   565    | const {Γ : List Expr} {c : Name} {ls ls' : List Level} :
   566        Level.eqList ls ls' = true → DefEq env Γ (const c ls) (const c ls')
   567    /-- `∀`-congruence (`DefEq.forallE`, `Rel.lean:399`): domains, then
   568    bodies under the RIGHT domain, and nothing else.  A
   569    `∀`'s value is a function of its domain's and its fibres' values
   570    (`SetLib.piV`: the propositional function space exactly when every fibre is
   571    a truth value), and both are types, never the point, so the
   572    premises' claims apply everywhere (`Sound.lean`, `DefEq.pi_sound`). -/
   573    | pi {Γ : List Expr} {A₁ B₁ A₂ B₂ : Expr} :
   574        DefEq env Γ A₁ A₂ → DefEq env (A₂ :: Γ) B₁ B₂ →
   575        DefEq env Γ (pi A₁ B₁) (pi A₂ B₂)
   576    /-- Lambda congruence (`DefEq.lams`, `Rel.lean:407`): domains, then
   577    bodies under the RIGHT domain — and, **typed**, the two
   578    bodies' inferred types under that domain are definitionally equal.
   579    A lambda's value is the point exactly when every body value is
   580    (`SetLib.lamV`), and a body may be a proof at some values of the
   581    variable and not at others (a large elimination into a family whose
   582    fibres are truth values at some indices); the claim on the bodies
   583    says nothing where one of them is the point, so the two bodies must
   584    lie in one type, whose members are all the point or none
   585    (`Sound.lean`, `DefEq.lam_sound`; without the premise the rule is
   586    unsound in this model, `ValueReading.lean`, `lam_congr_untyped_unsound`). -/
   587    | lam {Γ : List Expr} {A₁ b₁ A₂ b₂ t₁ t₂ : Expr} :
   588        DefEq env Γ A₁ A₂ → DefEq env (A₂ :: Γ) b₁ b₂ →
   589        Infer env (A₂ :: Γ) b₁ t₁ → Infer env (A₂ :: Γ) b₂ t₂ → DefEq env (A₂ :: Γ) t₁ t₂ →
   590        DefEq env Γ (lam A₁ b₁) (lam A₂ b₂)
   591    /-- **Lambda congruence over a propositional domain**: no
   592    comparison of the bodies' types.  The domain is a truth value, so it
   593    has at most one member, and a body's point-ness cannot vary with
   594    the variable: a lambda that is not the point has its one body value not
   595    the point, and the bodies' claim applies there (`Sound.lean`,
   596    `DefEq.lamProp_sound`).  The checker infers the domain's sort, not
   597    the bodies' types. -/
   598    | lamProp {Γ : List Expr} {A₁ b₁ A₂ b₂ s : Expr} {u : Level} :
   599        DefEq env Γ A₁ A₂ → DefEq env (A₂ :: Γ) b₁ b₂ →
   600        Infer env Γ A₂ s → Red env Γ s (sort u) → LevelOracle.eq u .zero = true →
   601        DefEq env Γ (lam A₁ b₁) (lam A₂ b₂)
   602    /-- **Lambda congruence of two constant bodies**: neither body
   603    uses the bound variable, so each body's value, and its point-ness,
   604    is the same at every value of the variable; a lambda that is not the
   605    point has a body that is not the point anywhere (`Sound.lean`,
   606    `DefEq.lamConst_sound`).  One constant body is not enough: the right
   607    body of `lam_congr_untyped_unsound` is the constant `n`. -/
   608    | lamConst {Γ : List Expr} {A₁ b₁ A₂ b₂ : Expr} :
   609        DefEq env Γ A₁ A₂ → DefEq env (A₂ :: Γ) b₁ b₂ →
   610        b₁.usesVar 0 = false → b₂.usesVar 0 = false →
   611        DefEq env Γ (lam A₁ b₁) (lam A₂ b₂)
   612    /-- **η over a propositional domain**: `DefEq.eta`
   613    without the lambda's body's type, for the reason of `lamProp`: over a
   614    domain with at most one member, the lambda and `b` that are not the point
   615    have their one body value not the point (`Sound.lean`,
   616    `DefEq.etaProp_sound`). -/
   617    | etaProp {Γ : List Expr} {A₁ b₁ b tb A₂ B s : Expr} {u : Level} :
   618        Infer env Γ b tb → Red env Γ tb (pi A₂ B) →
   619        DefEq env Γ A₂ A₁ →
   620        DefEq env (A₁ :: Γ) b₁ (app (b.liftN 1) (bvar 0)) →
   621        Infer env Γ A₁ s → Red env Γ s (sort u) → LevelOracle.eq u .zero = true →
   622        DefEq env Γ (lam A₁ b₁) b
   623    /-- **Application congruence at the head's type**: the
   624    heads are equal and the head's type reduces to a `∀` whose domain
   625    `S` is the arguments' common type, so the arguments are compared
   626    *at* `S` (`DefEqIn`) — lambda congruence and η between them need neither
   627    the bodies' types nor a domain comparison (`Sound.lean`,
   628    `DefEq.appIn_sound`).  The checker has the head's type for free when
   629    the head is a constant or a variable (con-leche's arguments of a
   630    constant-headed spine: the stored type instantiated along the
   631    earlier arguments). -/
   632    | appIn {Γ : List Expr} {f₁ a₁ f₂ a₂ tf S B : Expr} :
   633        DefEq env Γ f₁ f₂ → Infer env Γ f₁ tf → Red env Γ tf (pi S B) →
   634        DefEqIn env Γ S a₁ a₂ →
   635        DefEq env Γ (app f₁ a₁) (app f₂ a₂)
   636    /-- Application congruence (`DefEq.app`, `Rel.lean:412`). -/
   637    | app {Γ : List Expr} {f₁ a₁ f₂ a₂ : Expr} :
   638        DefEq env Γ f₁ f₂ → DefEq env Γ a₁ a₂ →
   639        DefEq env Γ (app f₁ a₁) (app f₂ a₂)
   640    /-- **η** (`DefEq.eta`, `Rel.lean:430`): a lambda against a term `b`
   641    whose inferred type reduces to a `∀` with a definitionally equal
   642    domain, when the lambda's body is `b` applied to the variable — and,
   643    **typed** as lambda congruence is, the lambda's body's inferred
   644    type is definitionally equal to the `∀`'s body, so that the lambda's body
   645    and `b` applied lie in one type.  Sound because a member of a
   646    function space is the abstraction of its applications
   647    (`SetLib.lamV_eta`). -/
   648    | eta {Γ : List Expr} {A₁ b₁ b tb A₂ B t₁ : Expr} :
   649        Infer env Γ b tb → Red env Γ tb (pi A₂ B) →
   650        DefEq env Γ A₂ A₁ →
   651        DefEq env (A₁ :: Γ) b₁ (app (b.liftN 1) (bvar 0)) →
   652        Infer env (A₁ :: Γ) b₁ t₁ → DefEq env (A₁ :: Γ) t₁ B →
   653        DefEq env Γ (lam A₁ b₁) b
   654    /-- **Proof irrelevance** (`DefEq.proofIrrel`, `Rel.lean:452`): both
   655    sides' inferred types have sort `Prop`.  **The two types are never
   656    compared**: the model justifies that, because every proof denotes the
   657    one point. -/
   658    | proofIrrel {Γ : List Expr} {a ta tta b tb ttb : Expr} {u v : Level} :
   659        Infer env Γ a ta → Infer env Γ ta tta → Red env Γ tta (sort u) →
   660        LevelOracle.eq u .zero = true →
   661        Infer env Γ b tb → Infer env Γ tb ttb → Red env Γ ttb (sort v) →
   662        LevelOracle.eq v .zero = true →
   663        DefEq env Γ a b
   664    /-- **Lambda telescope congruence**: a pair of lambda telescopes
   665    compared level by level, the bodies' types compared only at the
   666    innermost level (`DefEqLams`).  The checker's two-lambda arm skips the
   667    bodies' types exactly when both opened bodies are syntactically lambdas. -/
   668    | lams {Γ : List Expr} {a b : Expr} : DefEqLams env Γ a b → DefEq env Γ a b
   669  
   670  /-- **Lambda telescope congruence, typed at the innermost level only**.
   671  Two lambda telescopes are compared level by level: the domains
   672  at every level, the bodies' types only where the comparison stops
   673  descending through two lambdas.
   674  
   675  *Why the outer levels need no type comparison.*  Syntactically: the
   676  type of `fun x : A => fun y : B => c` is `∀ x : A, ∀ y : B, T` where
   677  `T` is `c`'s type, so for two telescopes compared with equal domains,
   678  each outer level's bodies' types are `∀`s over the domain the next
   679  level compares, with the next level's bodies' types as codomains; equal
   680  innermost bodies' types give equal bodies' types at every level, by
   681  `∀`-congruence.  Semantically (`Sound.lean`, `DefEqLams.outer_sound`):
   682  the type comparison is what makes lambda congruence's claim
   683  **unconditional** — `DefEq`'s claim says nothing where a side is the
   684  point, and two bodies in one type are both the point or neither — and
   685  an unconditional equality of the bodies at every value of the variable
   686  is an equality of the lambdas, with no type at all.  So the claim of this
   687  relation, `LamsSem`, is unconditional, and it propagates outward
   688  through any number of levels.
   689  
   690  *Unequal depth, and reduction between levels.*  The descent continues
   691  only through two **syntactic** lambdas (`outer`'s premise is this relation
   692  itself, which has no reduction rule).  Where one body is not a lambda — the
   693  comparison ends in η, or in any other rule, possibly after δ or whnf
   694  steps — that level is the innermost one (`inner`), and its bodies'
   695  types are inferred and compared at the full grade.  A δ or whnf step
   696  between levels therefore resets the accounting: the δ-witness `d :=
   697  fun x => (fun h => h) n` (`Probe.lean`, `lam_congr_sorts_unsound`)
   698  puts the reduction inside `inner`'s untyped premise `DefEq … b₁ b₂`,
   699  where the type comparison is still required.  Syntactically equal
   700  lambdas (`refl`) are equal outright. -/
   701  inductive DefEqLams (env : Env) : List Expr → Expr → Expr → Prop where
   702    /-- Syntactically equal sides (the checker's `a == b` fast path). -/
   703    | refl {Γ : List Expr} {a : Expr} : DefEqLams env Γ a a
   704    /-- The innermost level: `DefEq.lam`'s premises — domains, bodies,
   705    and the bodies' inferred types. -/
   706    | inner {Γ : List Expr} {A₁ b₁ A₂ b₂ t₁ t₂ : Expr} :
   707        DefEq env Γ A₁ A₂ → DefEq env (A₂ :: Γ) b₁ b₂ →
   708        Infer env (A₂ :: Γ) b₁ t₁ → Infer env (A₂ :: Γ) b₂ t₂ → DefEq env (A₂ :: Γ) t₁ t₂ →
   709        DefEqLams env Γ (lam A₁ b₁) (lam A₂ b₂)
   710    /-- An outer level: the domains, and the bodies by this relation —
   711    no inference, no type comparison. -/
   712    | outer {Γ : List Expr} {A₁ b₁ A₂ b₂ : Expr} :
   713        DefEq env Γ A₁ A₂ → DefEqLams env (A₂ :: Γ) b₁ b₂ →
   714        DefEqLams env Γ (lam A₁ b₁) (lam A₂ b₂)
   715  
   716  /-- **Comparison at a known type**: `a` and `b` are both
   717  members of `T` — the caller knows it, the relation does not check it —
   718  and the checker calls them definitionally equal.  Its claim is
   719  unconditional (`DefEqInSem`): a type's members are all the point or
   720  none, so the point needs no exception.  A lambda against a lambda, or against
   721  anything by η, is compared through the `∀` the type reduces to, at
   722  its body: the lambdas' domains are that `∀`'s (a graph in a function space
   723  has its domain), and the bodies lie in its fibres — no inference, no
   724  comparison of domains or of bodies' types. -/
   725  inductive DefEqIn (env : Env) : List Expr → Expr → Expr → Expr → Prop where
   726    /-- Any definitional equality, read at the common type. -/
   727    | of {Γ : List Expr} {T a b : Expr} : DefEq env Γ a b → DefEqIn env Γ T a b
   728    /-- Symmetry. -/
   729    | symm {Γ : List Expr} {T a b : Expr} : DefEqIn env Γ T a b → DefEqIn env Γ T b a
   730    /-- Lambda congruence at a `∀`: the bodies at its body. -/
   731    | lam {Γ : List Expr} {T D E A₁ b₁ A₂ b₂ : Expr} :
   732        Red env Γ T (pi D E) → DefEqIn env (A₂ :: Γ) E b₁ b₂ →
   733        DefEqIn env Γ T (lam A₁ b₁) (lam A₂ b₂)
   734    /-- η at a `∀`: the lambda's body against `b` applied, at its body. -/
   735    | eta {Γ : List Expr} {T D E A₁ b₁ b : Expr} :
   736        Red env Γ T (pi D E) → DefEqIn env (A₁ :: Γ) E b₁ (app (b.liftN 1) (bvar 0)) →
   737        DefEqIn env Γ T (lam A₁ b₁) b
   738  
   739  /-- **Type inference.** -/
   740  inductive Infer (env : Env) : List Expr → Expr → Expr → Prop where
   741    /-- A bound variable's type is its context entry, lifted over the
   742    binders in between (`Infer.fvar`, `Rel.lean:555`; the real checker
   743    reads the type off the free variable). -/
   744    | bvar {Γ : List Expr} {i : Nat} {A : Expr} :
   745        Γ[i]? = some A → Infer env Γ (bvar i) (A.liftN (i + 1))
   746    /-- `Sort u : Sort (u + 1)` (`Infer.sort`, `Rel.lean:551`). -/
   747    | sort {Γ : List Expr} {u : Level} :
   748        Infer env Γ (sort u) (sort (.succ u))
   749    /-- A stored constant at the right number of levels has its
   750    declared type, instantiated (`Infer.const`, `Rel.lean:559`). -/
   751    | const {Γ : List Expr} {c : Name} {ls : List Level} {ci : ConstInfo} :
   752        env.find? c = some ci → ls.length = ci.lparams.length →
   753        Infer env Γ (const c ls) (ci.type.instL ci.lparams ls)
   754    /-- **`∀`-formation** (`Infer.forallE`, `Rel.lean:576`): the domain's
   755    type reduces to a sort `u`, the body's type (under the domain)
   756    reduces to a sort `v`, the result is `Sort (imax u v)`.  Nothing is
   757    checked beyond Lean's own rule. -/
   758    | pi {Γ : List Expr} {A B s t : Expr} {u v : Level} :
   759        Infer env Γ A s → Red env Γ s (sort u) →
   760        Infer env (A :: Γ) B t → Red env (A :: Γ) t (sort v) →
   761        Infer env Γ (pi A B) (sort (.imax u v))
   762    /-- **Lambda** (`Infer.lam`, `Rel.lean:589`): the domain's type reduces to
   763    a sort, the body is inferred under the domain, and the result is the
   764    `∀` of the body's type — Lean's own rule.  The body's type's sort is
   765    not computed: an inferred type is a type (`InferSem`), which is all
   766    the `∀`'s invariant asks of it, and the body's value is read by the
   767    interpretation, not by its sort. -/
   768    | lam {Γ : List Expr} {A b s bt : Expr} {u : Level} :
   769        Infer env Γ A s → Red env Γ s (sort u) →
   770        Infer env (A :: Γ) b bt →
   771        Infer env Γ (lam A b) (pi A bt)
   772    /-- **Application** (`Infer.app`, `Rel.lean:617`): the head's type
   773    reduces to a `∀`, and the argument's inferred type is definitionally
   774    equal to its domain.  This is where a syntactic proof would need
   775    Π-injectivity and the semantic one does not: the `∀` the head's type
   776    reduces to *is* a function space, and membership in it is what the
   777    model needs (`Sound.lean`, `infer_sound`'s `app` case). -/
   778    | app {Γ : List Expr} {f a tf A B ta : Expr} :
   779        Infer env Γ f tf → Red env Γ tf (pi A B) →
   780        Infer env Γ a ta → DefEq env Γ ta A →
   781        Infer env Γ (app f a) (B.inst a)
   782    /-- **`let`, by substitution** (official `infer_let`
   783    with the body instantiated rather than opened at a let-variable, as
   784    the checker does): the type's type reduces to a
   785    sort, the value's inferred type is definitionally equal to the type,
   786    and the result is the inferred type of the body with the value
   787    substituted.  The two checks on the value are Lean's (they reject
   788    `let x : T := v; b` with `v : T` false even where the body ignores
   789    `x`); the soundness proof does not use them (`Sound.lean`,
   790    `Infer.letE_sound`), because `interp` reads no type and the body is
   791    inferred at the value itself. -/
   792    | letE {Γ : List Expr} {T v b s tv B : Expr} {u : Level} :
   793        Infer env Γ T s → Red env Γ s (sort u) →
   794        Infer env Γ v tv → DefEq env Γ tv T →
   795        Infer env Γ (b.inst v) B →
   796        Infer env Γ (letE T v b) B
   797  
   798  end

    97  mutual

    99  /-- **Reduction**: the head steps of `whnfCore` and the `whnf` loop,
   100  chained. -/
   101  inductive Red (env : Env) : Nat → Expr → Expr → Prop where

== whitepaper/Fragment/Rules.lean#L58-L69
    58  /-- **Reduction**: the head steps of the checker's `whnf`, chained. -/
    59  inductive Red (env : Env) : List Expr → Expr → Expr → Prop where
    60    /-- No step (`Red.refl`, `Rel.lean:106`). -/
    61    | refl {Γ : List Expr} {e : Expr} : Red env Γ e e
    62    /-- Chaining (`Red.trans`, `Rel.lean:111`).  A reduction is a
    63    denotation identity, so chaining costs nothing semantically. -/
    64    | trans {Γ : List Expr} {e₁ e₂ e₃ : Expr} :
    65        Red env Γ e₁ e₂ → Red env Γ e₂ e₃ → Red env Γ e₁ e₃
    66    /-- Head reduction inside an application (`Red.appFn`,
    67    `Rel.lean:116`): the head is reduced before a redex is looked for. -/
    68    | appFn {Γ : List Expr} {f f' a : Expr} :
    69        Red env Γ f f' → Red env Γ (app f a) (app f' a)

== ConLeche/Rules/Rel.lean#L101-L117
   101  inductive Red (env : Env) : Nat → Expr → Expr → Prop where
   102    /-- Every `pure e` exit: the value clauses of `whnfCoreBody`
   103    (`Kernel/Core.lean`), the stuck fallbacks (`:1003`, `:1033-1035`),
   104    an uncertified redex (`:1001`), `iotaRec = none` (`:1003`), the
   105    loop's fixpoint (`whnfStep`'s `pure e₁`, `:1088`). -/
   106    | refl {d : Nat} {e : Expr} : Red env d e e
   107    /-- The recursive `whnfCore` continuations after β/ι/proj
   108    (`Core.lean:990`, `:997`, `:1002`, `:1033`), the `whnf` loop
   109    (`whnfLoop`, `:1091-1095`), and the major's preparation chain
   110    (`prepareMajor`, `:785-807`). -/
   111    | trans {d : Nat} {e₁ e₂ e₃ : Expr} :
   112        Red env d e₁ e₂ → Red env d e₂ e₃ → Red env d e₁ e₃
   113    /-- Head normalisation inside an application (`whnfCoreBody`'s
   114    `.app` clause, `Kernel/Core.lean`: `whnfCore f` before the redex
   115    tests). -/
   116    | appFn {d : Nat} {f f' a : Expr} :
   117        Red env d f f' → Red env d (.app f a) (.app f' a)

== whitepaper/Fragment/Rules.lean#L70-L80
    70    /-- **β**: at every binder, with **no premise** — no
    71    inference of the argument, no comparison with the binder's domain.
    72    This is Lean's own β (`whnf_core`).  The model needs no premise
    73    (`Sound.lean`, `Red.beta_sound`): a reduction claims nothing of a
    74    redex that denotes the point, and a redex that does not has a lambda that
    75    does not, so a graph, which determines its domain: the argument lies
    76    in the lambda's domain because it lies in the domain of the slot the
    77    semantic invariant gives the application.
    78    -/
    79    | beta {Γ : List Expr} {A b a : Expr} :
    80        Red env Γ (app (lam A b) a) (b.inst a)

== whitepaper/Fragment/Rules.lean#L81-L87
    81    /-- **ζ**: a `let` reduces to its body with the value
    82    substituted, with no certificate, as β (con-leche's `whnfCore` on
    83    `.letE`, S0's `inst1M b v`; official `whnf_core`).  Unlike β it
    84    needs no case split on the point: the `let` and its reduct denote
    85    alike at every environment (`interp_zeta`). -/
    86    | zeta {Γ : List Expr} {T v b : Expr} :
    87        Red env Γ (letE T v b) (b.inst v)

== whitepaper/Fragment/Rules.lean#L547-L566
   547  inductive DefEq (env : Env) : List Expr → Expr → Expr → Prop where
   548    /-- The syntactic fast path (`DefEq.refl`, `Rel.lean:362`). -/
   549    | refl {Γ : List Expr} {a : Expr} : DefEq env Γ a a
   550    /-- Symmetry (`DefEq.symm`, `Rel.lean:365`).  Not a checker move: the
   551    constructor from which every right-hand variant of a one-sided rule
   552    is derived. -/
   553    | symm {Γ : List Expr} {a b : Expr} : DefEq env Γ a b → DefEq env Γ b a
   554    /-- **Reduce the left side, then continue** (`DefEq.redL`,
   555    `Rel.lean:370`): the recursive structure of `isDefEq` — head
   556    normalisation of either side (with `symm`) and every lazy-δ
   557    continuation. -/
   558    | redL {Γ : List Expr} {a a' b : Expr} :
   559        Red env Γ a a' → DefEq env Γ a' b → DefEq env Γ a b
   560    /-- Two sorts, by the level oracle (`DefEq.sort`, `Rel.lean:373`). -/
   561    | sort {Γ : List Expr} {u v : Level} :
   562        LevelOracle.eq u v = true → DefEq env Γ (sort u) (sort v)
   563    /-- Two constants of the same name at oracle-equal levels
   564    (`DefEq.const`, `Rel.lean:384`). -/
   565    | const {Γ : List Expr} {c : Name} {ls ls' : List Level} :
   566        Level.eqList ls ls' = true → DefEq env Γ (const c ls) (const c ls')

== ConLeche/Rules/Rel.lean#L372-L374
   372    /-- Two sorts (`Core.lean:1581`). -/
   373    | sort {d : Nat} {u v : Level} :
   374        Level.isEquiv u v = some true → DefEq env d (.sort u) (.sort v)

== whitepaper/Fragment/Rules.lean#L567-L575
   567    /-- `∀`-congruence (`DefEq.forallE`, `Rel.lean:399`): domains, then
   568    bodies under the RIGHT domain, and nothing else.  A
   569    `∀`'s value is a function of its domain's and its fibres' values
   570    (`SetLib.piV`: the propositional function space exactly when every fibre is
   571    a truth value), and both are types, never the point, so the
   572    premises' claims apply everywhere (`Sound.lean`, `DefEq.pi_sound`). -/
   573    | pi {Γ : List Expr} {A₁ B₁ A₂ B₂ : Expr} :
   574        DefEq env Γ A₁ A₂ → DefEq env (A₂ :: Γ) B₁ B₂ →
   575        DefEq env Γ (pi A₁ B₁) (pi A₂ B₂)

== whitepaper/Fragment/Rules.lean#L701-L714
   701  inductive DefEqLams (env : Env) : List Expr → Expr → Expr → Prop where
   702    /-- Syntactically equal sides (the checker's `a == b` fast path). -/
   703    | refl {Γ : List Expr} {a : Expr} : DefEqLams env Γ a a
   704    /-- The innermost level: `DefEq.lam`'s premises — domains, bodies,
   705    and the bodies' inferred types. -/
   706    | inner {Γ : List Expr} {A₁ b₁ A₂ b₂ t₁ t₂ : Expr} :
   707        DefEq env Γ A₁ A₂ → DefEq env (A₂ :: Γ) b₁ b₂ →
   708        Infer env (A₂ :: Γ) b₁ t₁ → Infer env (A₂ :: Γ) b₂ t₂ → DefEq env (A₂ :: Γ) t₁ t₂ →
   709        DefEqLams env Γ (lam A₁ b₁) (lam A₂ b₂)
   710    /-- An outer level: the domains, and the bodies by this relation —
   711    no inference, no type comparison. -/
   712    | outer {Γ : List Expr} {A₁ b₁ A₂ b₂ : Expr} :
   713        DefEq env Γ A₁ A₂ → DefEqLams env (A₂ :: Γ) b₁ b₂ →
   714        DefEqLams env Γ (lam A₁ b₁) (lam A₂ b₂)

== whitepaper/Fragment/Rules.lean#L704-L709
   704    /-- The innermost level: `DefEq.lam`'s premises — domains, bodies,
   705    and the bodies' inferred types. -/
   706    | inner {Γ : List Expr} {A₁ b₁ A₂ b₂ t₁ t₂ : Expr} :
   707        DefEq env Γ A₁ A₂ → DefEq env (A₂ :: Γ) b₁ b₂ →
   708        Infer env (A₂ :: Γ) b₁ t₁ → Infer env (A₂ :: Γ) b₂ t₂ → DefEq env (A₂ :: Γ) t₁ t₂ →
   709        DefEqLams env Γ (lam A₁ b₁) (lam A₂ b₂)

== whitepaper/Fragment/Rules.lean#L640-L653
   640    /-- **η** (`DefEq.eta`, `Rel.lean:430`): a lambda against a term `b`
   641    whose inferred type reduces to a `∀` with a definitionally equal
   642    domain, when the lambda's body is `b` applied to the variable — and,
   643    **typed** as lambda congruence is, the lambda's body's inferred
   644    type is definitionally equal to the `∀`'s body, so that the lambda's body
   645    and `b` applied lie in one type.  Sound because a member of a
   646    function space is the abstraction of its applications
   647    (`SetLib.lamV_eta`). -/
   648    | eta {Γ : List Expr} {A₁ b₁ b tb A₂ B t₁ : Expr} :
   649        Infer env Γ b tb → Red env Γ tb (pi A₂ B) →
   650        DefEq env Γ A₂ A₁ →
   651        DefEq env (A₁ :: Γ) b₁ (app (b.liftN 1) (bvar 0)) →
   652        Infer env (A₁ :: Γ) b₁ t₁ → DefEq env (A₁ :: Γ) t₁ B →
   653        DefEq env Γ (lam A₁ b₁) b

== whitepaper/Fragment/Rules.lean#L654-L663
   654    /-- **Proof irrelevance** (`DefEq.proofIrrel`, `Rel.lean:452`): both
   655    sides' inferred types have sort `Prop`.  **The two types are never
   656    compared**: the model justifies that, because every proof denotes the
   657    one point. -/
   658    | proofIrrel {Γ : List Expr} {a ta tta b tb ttb : Expr} {u v : Level} :
   659        Infer env Γ a ta → Infer env Γ ta tta → Red env Γ tta (sort u) →
   660        LevelOracle.eq u .zero = true →
   661        Infer env Γ b tb → Infer env Γ tb ttb → Red env Γ ttb (sort v) →
   662        LevelOracle.eq v .zero = true →
   663        DefEq env Γ a b

== whitepaper/Fragment/Rules.lean#L529-L546
   529  /-- **Definitional equality**: the verdict `true` of the checker's
   530  `isDefEq`.
   531  
   532  **There is no `trans` rule, deliberately** (`Rel.lean:334-357`).
   533  The relation is the checker's verdict on two terms that are
   534  well-formed *together*, a fact no rule states because well-formedness
   535  is semantic (`WellDenoted`) and may not enter this inductive.  Every
   536  rule respects one discipline instead: **the subject of each `DefEq`
   537  premise is a subterm of the conclusion or is produced by a `Red` or
   538  `Infer` premise** (a reduct, an inferred type), so the soundness proof
   539  always has the premise's terms — and their invariant — in hand.  A
   540  `trans` rule is the unique rule that would break it: its middle term
   541  comes from nowhere, so nothing supplies its invariant, and the
   542  induction has nothing to apply the hypothesis to.  Nor does the
   543  checker chain through an arbitrary middle term: every comparison it
   544  makes is one of the rules below, and its one way to chain is
   545  "reduce, then continue": `redL`.
   546  -/

== ConLeche/Rules/Rel.lean#L334-L357
   334  /-- **Definitional equality**: the verdict `true` of `isDefEq`.
   335  
   336  **There is no `trans` rule, deliberately, and none can be added**
   337  (task #309, the experiment recorded in DESIGN.md).  The relation is
   338  not an equivalence on terms: it is the checker's verdict, and the
   339  checker only ever compares terms that are well-formed *together* — a
   340  fact the rules never state, because well-formedness (scoping, the
   341  readability of the terms, the grading of the reading) is semantic
   342  and may not enter this inductive.  Every rule respects one syntactic
   343  discipline instead: **the subject of each `DefEq` premise is either a
   344  subterm of the conclusion or is produced by an existence-form `Red` /
   345  `Infer` premise** (a reduct, an inferred type), so the soundness proof
   346  (`ConLeche/Model/Rules/Sound.lean`) always has the premise's terms in
   347  hand.  `trans` is the unique rule that would break it: its middle
   348  term comes from nowhere, and with it two rules that are each sound
   349  alone meet — `fvar` compares free variables by index only (their
   350  types are not compared, as the checker does not), while
   351  `proofFast` *reads* a head's stored data to decide "definitely a
   352  proof" — and derive `DefEq env d (.fvar i ty) (.fvar i' ty')` for
   353  every `i`, `i'`, which no model satisfies.  The recursive-structure rules
   354  (`redL`, `natSucc`, `eta`, `structUnit`) are therefore not a
   355  proof-engineering convenience but what keeps the relation sound; the
   356  one chaining that is sound, "reduce, then continue", is `redL`, and
   357  its right-hand and δ variants are derived in `Derived.lean`. -/

== ConLeche/Rules/Rel.lean#L375-L381
   375    /-- Two free variables of the same index (`Kernel/Core.lean`).  The
   376    carried types are NOT compared, as the checker does not compare them:
   377    at a well-formed call `CtxOk` pins every opened variable's type, so
   378    the reading ignores them.  This is one half of why the relation has
   379    no `trans` (see the inductive's docstring). -/
   380    | fvar {d i : Nat} {ty₁ ty₂ : Expr} :
   381        DefEq env d (.fvar i ty₁) (.fvar i ty₂)

== ConLeche/Rules/Rel.lean#L439-L445
   439    /-- **The `isProofFast` yes-arm** (`propIrrel`, `Kernel/Core.lean`):
   440    both heads' stored data say "a proposition at every valuation"
   441    (`prf_of_isProofFast`). -/
   442    | proofFast {d : Nat} {a b : Expr} :
   443        isProofFast env.find? env.findTable? a = true →
   444          isProofFast env.find? env.findTable? b = true →
   445        DefEq env d a b

== whitepaper/Fragment/Rules.lean#L740-L748
   740  inductive Infer (env : Env) : List Expr → Expr → Expr → Prop where
   741    /-- A bound variable's type is its context entry, lifted over the
   742    binders in between (`Infer.fvar`, `Rel.lean:555`; the real checker
   743    reads the type off the free variable). -/
   744    | bvar {Γ : List Expr} {i : Nat} {A : Expr} :
   745        Γ[i]? = some A → Infer env Γ (bvar i) (A.liftN (i + 1))
   746    /-- `Sort u : Sort (u + 1)` (`Infer.sort`, `Rel.lean:551`). -/
   747    | sort {Γ : List Expr} {u : Level} :
   748        Infer env Γ (sort u) (sort (.succ u))

== ConLeche/Rules/Rel.lean#L550-L566
   550  inductive Infer (env : Env) : Grade → Nat → Expr → Expr → Prop where
   551    /-- `Core.lean:1114` / `:1294`. -/
   552    | sort {g : Grade} {d : Nat} {u : Level} :
   553        Infer env g d (.sort u) (.sort (.succ u))
   554    /-- `Kernel/Core.lean` / `:1295-1297`: an opened variable's stored
   555    type, at the leaf scope check. -/
   556    | fvar {g : Grade} {d idx : Nat} {ty : Expr} :
   557        idx < d → Infer env g d (.fvar idx ty) ty
   558    /-- `Kernel/Core.lean` / `:1298-1309`: a stored constant at the right
   559    level arity. -/
   560    | const {g : Grade} {d : Nat} {n : Name} {us : List Level}
   561        {ci : ConstantInfo} :
   562        env.find? n = some ci →
   563        us.length = ci.toConstantVal.levelParams.length →
   564        Infer env g d (.const n us)
   565          (ci.toConstantVal.type.instantiateLevelParams
   566            ci.toConstantVal.levelParams us)

== whitepaper/Fragment/Rules.lean#L754-L771
   754    /-- **`∀`-formation** (`Infer.forallE`, `Rel.lean:576`): the domain's
   755    type reduces to a sort `u`, the body's type (under the domain)
   756    reduces to a sort `v`, the result is `Sort (imax u v)`.  Nothing is
   757    checked beyond Lean's own rule. -/
   758    | pi {Γ : List Expr} {A B s t : Expr} {u v : Level} :
   759        Infer env Γ A s → Red env Γ s (sort u) →
   760        Infer env (A :: Γ) B t → Red env (A :: Γ) t (sort v) →
   761        Infer env Γ (pi A B) (sort (.imax u v))
   762    /-- **Lambda** (`Infer.lam`, `Rel.lean:589`): the domain's type reduces to
   763    a sort, the body is inferred under the domain, and the result is the
   764    `∀` of the body's type — Lean's own rule.  The body's type's sort is
   765    not computed: an inferred type is a type (`InferSem`), which is all
   766    the `∀`'s invariant asks of it, and the body's value is read by the
   767    interpretation, not by its sort. -/
   768    | lam {Γ : List Expr} {A b s bt : Expr} {u : Level} :
   769        Infer env Γ A s → Red env Γ s (sort u) →
   770        Infer env (A :: Γ) b bt →
   771        Infer env Γ (lam A b) (pi A bt)

== whitepaper/Fragment/Rules.lean#L772-L781
   772    /-- **Application** (`Infer.app`, `Rel.lean:617`): the head's type
   773    reduces to a `∀`, and the argument's inferred type is definitionally
   774    equal to its domain.  This is where a syntactic proof would need
   775    Π-injectivity and the semantic one does not: the `∀` the head's type
   776    reduces to *is* a function space, and membership in it is what the
   777    model needs (`Sound.lean`, `infer_sound`'s `app` case). -/
   778    | app {Γ : List Expr} {f a tf A B ta : Expr} :
   779        Infer env Γ f tf → Red env Γ tf (pi A B) →
   780        Infer env Γ a ta → DefEq env Γ ta A →
   781        Infer env Γ (app f a) (B.inst a)

== ConLeche/Rules/Rel.lean#L618-L622
   618    | app {g : Grade} {d : Nat} {f a tf ty body ta : Expr} :
   619        Infer env g d f tf → Red env d tf (.forallE ty body) →
   620        (g = .full → Infer env .full d a ta) →
   621        (g = .full → DefEq env d ta ty) →
   622        Infer env g d (.app f a) (body.instantiate1 a)

== whitepaper/Fragment/Rules.lean#L782-L796
   782    /-- **`let`, by substitution** (official `infer_let`
   783    with the body instantiated rather than opened at a let-variable, as
   784    the checker does): the type's type reduces to a
   785    sort, the value's inferred type is definitionally equal to the type,
   786    and the result is the inferred type of the body with the value
   787    substituted.  The two checks on the value are Lean's (they reject
   788    `let x : T := v; b` with `v : T` false even where the body ignores
   789    `x`); the soundness proof does not use them (`Sound.lean`,
   790    `Infer.letE_sound`), because `interp` reads no type and the body is
   791    inferred at the value itself. -/
   792    | letE {Γ : List Expr} {T v b s tv B : Expr} {u : Level} :
   793        Infer env Γ T s → Red env Γ s (sort u) →
   794        Infer env Γ v tv → DefEq env Γ tv T →
   795        Infer env Γ (b.inst v) B →
   796        Infer env Γ (letE T v b) B

== ConLeche/Kernel/Core.lean#L979-L981
   979      | .letE _ v b =>
   980        -- Task #342 S0: ζ
   981        r.whnfCore cheap depth (b.instantiate1 v)

== ConLeche/Kernel/Core.lean#L1175-L1180
  1175      | .letE ty v b => do
  1176        -- Task #342 S0: official `infer_let`
  1177        let _ ← ensureSort r env depth (← r.infer depth ty)
  1178        unless ← r.defeq depth (← r.infer depth v) ty do
  1179          throw (.invalid "let value type mismatch")
  1180        r.infer depth (b.instantiate1 v)

>>> whitepaper/sections/02b-model-proof.typ

== whitepaper/Fragment/Lib.lean#L56-L126
    56  /-- **The set theory we assume.**  A type of sets `V` with the
    57  operators and laws the fragment's proof uses.  The theory is stated in
    58  Lean's logic, so separation is available for every predicate of that
    59  logic, and the function-space laws quantify over functions on the
    60  sets. -/
    61  class SetLib (V : Type u) where
    62    /-- Membership. -/
    63    Mem : V → V → Prop
    64    /-- Extensionality. -/
    65    ext : ∀ {x y : V}, (∀ z, Mem z x ↔ Mem z y) → x = y
    66    /-- Separation: the members of `A` that satisfy `P`. -/
    67    sep : V → (V → Prop) → V
    68    /-- The members of a separation. -/
    69    mem_sep : ∀ {A : V} {P : V → Prop} {z : V}, Mem z (sep A P) ↔ Mem z A ∧ P z
    70    /-- A distinguished set, subject to the point's three laws below.  It
    71    is the one proof of every true proposition. -/
    72    pt : V
    73    /-- The one-element set `{pt}`. -/
    74    one : V
    75    /-- The members of `{pt}`. -/
    76    mem_one : ∀ {z : V}, Mem z one ↔ z = pt
    77    /-- The universe chain: `univ n` sizes `Sort n`, which denotes the
    78    types among its members, `typeU n`. -/
    79    univ : Nat → V
    80    /-- `univ 0` is the set of subsets of `{pt}` — the truth values. -/
    81    mem_univ_zero : ∀ {T : V}, Mem T (univ 0) ↔ ∀ z, Mem z T → z = pt
    82    /-- Each universe is a member of the next. -/
    83    univ_mem_succ : ∀ n : Nat, Mem (univ n) (univ (n + 1))
    84    /-- Cumulativity. -/
    85    univ_mono : ∀ {m n : Nat} {x : V}, m ≤ n → Mem x (univ m) → Mem x (univ n)
    86    /-- The graph of a function on a domain. -/
    87    graph : (V → V) → V → V
    88    /-- The dependent function space: the graphs over `A` with values
    89    in the fibres `B`. -/
    90    piSet : V → (V → V) → V
    91    /-- Application.  On the point it is the point (a proof applied to
    92    anything is a proof); on a graph it reads the graph. -/
    93    app : V → V → V
    94    /-- A proof applied is the proof. -/
    95    app_pt : ∀ a : V, app pt a = pt
    96    /-- β: a graph applied on its domain computes. -/
    97    app_graph : ∀ {F : V → V} {A a : V}, Mem a A → app (graph F A) a = F a
    98    /-- A graph is never the point. -/
    99    graph_ne_pt : ∀ {F : V → V} {A : V}, graph F A ≠ pt
   100    /-- A graph depends only on the function's values on the domain. -/
   101    graph_congr : ∀ {F F' : V → V} {A : V}, (∀ x, Mem x A → F x = F' x) → graph F A = graph F' A
   102    /-- A function space depends only on the fibres over the domain. -/
   103    piSet_congr : ∀ {A : V} {B B' : V → V}, (∀ x, Mem x A → B x = B' x) → piSet A B = piSet A B'
   104    /-- Introduction: fibre-wise members abstract into the space. -/
   105    graph_mem_piSet : ∀ {A : V} {F B : V → V},
   106      (∀ x, Mem x A → Mem (F x) (B x)) → Mem (graph F A) (piSet A B)
   107    /-- Elimination. -/
   108    app_mem_piSet : ∀ {A f a : V} {B : V → V}, Mem f (piSet A B) → Mem a A → Mem (app f a) (B a)
   109    /-- η: a member of a function space is the graph of its applications. -/
   110    graph_app_eq : ∀ {A f : V} {B : V → V}, Mem f (piSet A B) → graph (fun x => app f x) A = f
   111    /-- A graph determines its domain. -/
   112    piSet_dom_unique : ∀ {A A' f : V} {B B' : V → V},
   113      Mem f (piSet A B) → Mem f (piSet A' B') → A = A'
   114    /-- Closure of the positive universes under dependent function
   115    spaces. -/
   116    piSet_mem_univ : ∀ {n : Nat} {A : V} {B : V → V}, n ≠ 0 →
   117      Mem A (univ n) → (∀ x, Mem x A → Mem (B x) (univ n)) → Mem (piSet A B) (univ n)
   118    /-- Closure of the universes under separation. -/
   119    sep_mem_univ : ∀ {n : Nat} {A : V} {P : V → Prop}, Mem A (univ n) → Mem (sep A P) (univ n)
   120    /-- **The point's laws** (1): the point is not a truth value — it has
   121    a member other than itself. -/
   122    pt_not_mem_univ_zero : ¬ Mem pt (univ 0)
   123    /-- (2): the point has at most one member. -/
   124    pt_subsingleton : ∀ {x y : V}, Mem x pt → Mem y pt → x = y
   125    /-- (3): no graph is a member of the point. -/
   126    graph_not_mem_pt : ∀ {F : V → V} {A : V}, ¬ Mem (graph F A) pt

== ConLeche/SetTheory/Core.lean#L95-L100
    95  /-- A model of set theory of exactly the strength the checker needs:
    96  membership, the six ZF⁻ axioms (extensionality, pairing, union, power
    97  set, regularity, Lean-level replacement), and an ω-chain of
    98  Grothendieck universes.  Infinity is derivable; choice is inherited
    99  from the meta-logic (`Classical.choice`); see the module docstring. -/
   100  class SetTheory (V : Type u) where

== whitepaper/Fragment/Lib.lean#L275-L278
   275  /-- **Impredicativity**: a function space landing in `Prop` is a truth value,
   276  whatever its domain. -/
   277  theorem piR_true_mem_univ_zero {A : V} {B : V → V} :

== whitepaper/Fragment/Interp.lean#L138-L146
   138  /-- **The interpretation**: total, term-directed, reading no type. -/
   139  noncomputable def interp (M : Name → List Nat → V) (φ : Name → Nat) : (Nat → V) → Expr → V
   140    | ρ, .bvar i => ρ i
   141    | _, .sort u => typeU (u.eval φ)
   142    | _, .const c ls => M c (ls.map (Level.eval φ))
   143    | ρ, .app f a => app (interp M φ ρ f) (interp M φ ρ a)
   144    | ρ, .lam A b => lamV (interp M φ ρ A) fun x => interp M φ (cons x ρ) b
   145    | ρ, .pi A B => piV (interp M φ ρ A) fun x => interp M φ (cons x ρ) B
   146    | ρ, .letE _ v b => interp M φ (cons (interp M φ ρ v) ρ) b

== whitepaper/Fragment/Lib.lean#L469-L481
   469  open Classical in
   470  /-- Is every fibre over the domain a truth value? -/
   471  noncomputable def propB (A : V) (B : V → V) : Bool := decide (∀ x, x ∈ˢ A → B x ∈ˢ univ 0)
   472  
   473  open Classical in
   474  /-- Is every body value over the domain the point? -/
   475  noncomputable def ptB (A : V) (F : V → V) : Bool := decide (∀ x, x ∈ˢ A → F x = pt)
   476  
   477  /-- **The function space, regime read off the fibres.** -/
   478  noncomputable def piV (A : V) (B : V → V) : V := piR (propB A B) A B
   479  
   480  /-- **The abstraction, regime read off the body values.** -/
   481  noncomputable def lamV (A : V) (F : V → V) : V := lamR (ptB A F) A F

== whitepaper/Fragment/Lib.lean#L185-L191
   185  /-- **The propositional function space** `Π₀(A, B)`: the truth value "every
   186  fibre is `{pt}`".  When the fibres are truth values it is their
   187  intersection `⋂ x ∈ A, B x` (the empty intersection being `{pt}`):
   188  `{pt}` exactly when every fibre is, `∅` otherwise — the function space of
   189  subsets of a singleton.  Reducible, so proofs that unfold `piR true`
   190  keep working. -/
   191  abbrev piProp (A : V) (B : V → V) : V := truthVal (∀ x, x ∈ˢ A → B x = one)

== whitepaper/Fragment/Lib.lean#L625-L631
   625  /-- Over an empty domain the function space is `{pt}`. -/
   626  theorem piV_of_empty {A : V} {B : V → V} (h : ∀ x, ¬ x ∈ˢ A) : piV A B = one := by
   627    unfold piV
   628    rw [propB_eq_true.mpr fun x hx => absurd hx (h x), piR_true]
   629    exact ext fun z => by
   630      rw [mem_truthVal, mem_one]
   631      exact ⟨fun h' => h'.1, fun h' => ⟨h', fun x hx => absurd hx (h x)⟩⟩

== whitepaper/Fragment/Lib.lean#L633-L635
   633  /-- Over an empty domain the abstraction is the point. -/
   634  theorem lamV_of_empty {A : V} {F : V → V} (h : ∀ x, ¬ x ∈ˢ A) : lamV A F = pt :=
   635    lamV_eq_pt fun x hx => absurd hx (h x)

    53  truth value `{pt}`, although its sort is `Type`. -/
    54  theorem piV_const_one {A : V} : piV A (fun _ => one) = one := by

== whitepaper/Fragment/Lib.lean#L298-L302
   298  /-- A **strict** set: not the point, and the point is not a member. -/
   299  def Strict (X : V) : Prop := X ≠ pt ∧ ¬ pt ∈ˢ X
   300  
   301  /-- A **type**: a truth value, or a strict set. -/
   302  def IsTy (X : V) : Prop := X ∈ˢ univ 0 ∨ Strict X

== whitepaper/Fragment/Lib.lean#L359-L364
   359  /-- The members of a type are all the point or none of them. -/
   360  theorem IsTy.eq_of_ne_pt {T x y : V} (hT : IsTy T) (hx : x ∈ˢ T) (hy : y ∈ˢ T)
   361      (h : x ≠ pt → y ≠ pt → x = y) : x = y := by
   362    rcases hT with hT | hT
   363    · rw [eq_pt_of_mem_univ_zero hT hx, eq_pt_of_mem_univ_zero hT hy]
   364    · exact h (ne_pt_of_mem_strict hT hx) (ne_pt_of_mem_strict hT hy)

== whitepaper/Fragment/Lib.lean#L304-L306
   304  /-- **What `Sort n` denotes**: the truth values at `0`, the members of
   305  `univ n` that are types above. -/
   306  def typeU (n : Nat) : V := if n = 0 then univ 0 else sep (univ n) IsTy

== whitepaper/Fragment/ValueReading.lean#L58-L63
    58  /-- A function space over an empty domain is `{pt}`, which is no strict set;
    59  so a positive sort, which holds `False → Nat`, holds a set that is not
    60  strict. -/
    61  theorem piV_empty_not_strict {A : V} {B : V → V} (h : ∀ x, ¬ x ∈ˢ A) :
    62      ¬ Strict (piV A B) := by
    63    rw [piV_of_empty h]; exact fun hs => hs.2 (mem_one.mpr rfl)

== whitepaper/Fragment/WellDenoted.lean#L55-L78
    55  /-- **The semantic invariant** (see the module docstring): a binder's
    56  domain is a type; a binder's codomain fibres are types; an application
    57  in the graph regime has a type as its slot's domain. -/
    58  def WellDenoted : (Nat → V) → Expr → Prop
    59    | _, .bvar _ => True
    60    | _, .sort _ => True
    61    | _, .const _ _ => True
    62    | ρ, .app f a =>
    63      WellDenoted ρ f ∧ WellDenoted ρ a ∧
    64        ∃ (p : Bool) (A : V) (B : V → V),
    65          interp M φ ρ f ∈ˢ piR p A B ∧ interp M φ ρ a ∈ˢ A ∧
    66          (p = true → ∀ x, x ∈ˢ A → B x ∈ˢ univ 0) ∧ (p = false → IsTy A)
    67    | ρ, .lam A b =>
    68      WellDenoted ρ A ∧ IsTy (interp M φ ρ A) ∧
    69        (∀ x, x ∈ˢ interp M φ ρ A → WellDenoted (cons x ρ) b) ∧
    70        ∃ B : V → V,
    71          (∀ x, x ∈ˢ interp M φ ρ A → interp M φ (cons x ρ) b ∈ˢ B x) ∧
    72          (∀ x, x ∈ˢ interp M φ ρ A → IsTy (B x))
    73    | ρ, .pi A B =>
    74      WellDenoted ρ A ∧ IsTy (interp M φ ρ A) ∧
    75        (∀ x, x ∈ˢ interp M φ ρ A → WellDenoted (cons x ρ) B) ∧
    76        (∀ x, x ∈ˢ interp M φ ρ A → IsTy (interp M φ (cons x ρ) B))
    77    | ρ, .letE _ v b =>
    78      WellDenoted ρ v ∧ WellDenoted (cons (interp M φ ρ v) ρ) b

== whitepaper/Fragment/Lib.lean#L552-L558
   552  /-- **Introduction**: body values in fibres that are types abstract into
   553  the function space.  Where every fibre is a truth value every body value is
   554  the point, and so is the abstraction; where one fibre is not, it is
   555  strict, its body value is not the point, and the abstraction is the
   556  graph. -/
   557  theorem lamV_mem {A : V} {F B : V → V} (hF : ∀ x, x ∈ˢ A → F x ∈ˢ B x)
   558      (hB : ∀ x, x ∈ˢ A → IsTy (B x)) : lamV A F ∈ˢ piV A B := by

== whitepaper/Fragment/WellDenoted.lean#L196-L199
   196  theorem WellDenoted_inst0 {e a : Expr} {ρ : Nat → V} (ha : WellDenoted M φ ρ a) :
   197      WellDenoted M φ ρ (e.inst a) ↔ WellDenoted M φ (cons (interp M φ ρ a) ρ) e := by
   198    have h := WellDenoted_inst M φ e a 0 ρ (by rwa [shiftE_zero_zero])
   199    rwa [shiftE_zero_zero, instE_zero] at h

== whitepaper/Fragment/WellDenoted.lean#L252-L259
   252  /-- **Satisfaction of a context**: every entry is a well-denoted type
   253  under the environment beyond it, and the variable's value is a member
   254  of it.  The semantic `Γ ⊢`. -/
   255  def Sat : List Expr → (Nat → V) → Prop
   256    | [], _ => True
   257    | A :: Γ, ρ =>
   258      Sat Γ (fun i => ρ (i + 1)) ∧ WellDenoted M φ (fun i => ρ (i + 1)) A ∧
   259        IsTy (interp M φ (fun i => ρ (i + 1)) A) ∧ ρ 0 ∈ˢ interp M φ (fun i => ρ (i + 1)) A

== whitepaper/Fragment/Sound.lean#L107-L132
   107  /-- **β at every binder, with no premise** — `beta_of_ne_pt`.  The
   108  redex is not the point, so neither is its lambda; a lambda that is not the point
   109  is the graph of its body; and the graph's domain is the slot's: the
   110  argument is in it. -/
   111  theorem beta_sound {Γ : List Expr} {A b a : Expr} :
   112      RedSem m φ Γ (.app (.lam A b) a) (b.inst a) := by
   113    intro ρ _ hw hn
   114    rw [WellDenoted_app] at hw
   115    obtain ⟨hl, ha, p, A', B', hslot, hmem, -, -⟩ := hw
   116    rw [WellDenoted_lam] at hl
   117    obtain ⟨-, -, hbody, B, hfib, -⟩ := hl
   118    have hlam := fn_ne_pt hn
   119    have hval : interp m.M φ ρ (.lam A b) =
   120        graph (fun x => interp m.M φ (cons x ρ) b) (interp m.M φ ρ A) := by
   121      rw [interp_lam] at hlam ⊢; exact lamV_eq_graph hlam
   122    have hp : p = false := by
   123      cases p
   124      · rfl
   125      · exact absurd (eq_pt_of_mem_piR_true hslot) hlam
   126    subst hp
   127    have hown : interp m.M φ ρ (.lam A b) ∈ˢ piR false (interp m.M φ ρ A) B := by
   128      rw [hval, piR_false]; exact graph_mem_piSet hfib
   129    have haA : interp m.M φ ρ a ∈ˢ interp m.M φ ρ A := by
   130      rw [piR_dom_unique hown hslot]; exact hmem
   131    refine ⟨(WellDenoted_inst0 m.M φ ha).mpr (hbody _ haA), ?_⟩
   132    rw [interp_app, interp_lam, app_lamV haA, interp_inst0]

== whitepaper/Fragment/EtaIota.lean#L707-L724
   707  open EtaWit in
   708  /-- **Eta on the reduct of the major is outside the claims**.
   709  The major `maj := (fun x : A => g (k x)) a` is well-denoted
   710  and the point (a lambda that is the point constrains nothing, so `a` may
   711  lie outside `A`), and it β-reduces to `maj' := g (k a)`, which is not
   712  well-denoted (`k` is a graph over `A`).  The redex `rec minor maj` is
   713  well-denoted and not the point.  Eta-expanding the major's reduct,
   714  `minor (p0 maj')`, breaks the reduction claim; eta-expanding the major
   715  as it stands, `minor (p0 maj)`, satisfies it.  So the checker's eta
   716  path must not reduce the major first (lean4#15371 expands before the
   717  major's `whnf`). -/
   718  theorem etaIota_reduced_major_witness [LevelOracle] (φ : Name → Nat) (env : Env)
   719      (Γ : List Expr) :
   720      Red env Γ maj maj' ∧
   721      (∀ ρ : Nat → V, WellDenoted (witM (V := V)) φ ρ redex2 ∧ interp witM φ ρ redex2 ≠ pt ∧
   722        interp witM φ ρ maj = pt) ∧
   723      ¬ RedSem (EnvModel.empty (witM (V := V))) φ [] redex2 etaRed2 ∧
   724      RedSem (EnvModel.empty (witM (V := V))) φ [] redex2 eta2 := by
