== whitepaper/Fragment/Access.lean#L68-L78
    68  /-- **Accessibility with the bound `A`** of an operator from families
    69  over `ι` to families over `κ`: every element `x` the operator
    70  produces at `j` from a family `W` in the universe has a support — a
    71  subset `B` of `A` and occurrences `g a ∈ W` for `a ∈ B` — such that
    72  `x` is produced at `j` from every family `W'` in the universe
    73  containing the support.  Con-leche: `AccTuple`,
    74  `ConLeche/SetModel/Access.lean`. -/
    75  def AccFam (n : Nat) (Φ : (ι → V) → κ → V) (A : V) : Prop :=
    76    ∀ W, InUniv n W → ∀ j x, x ∈ˢ Φ W j →
    77      ∃ (B : V) (g : V → ι × V), B ⊆ˢ A ∧ (∀ a, a ∈ˢ B → InFam W (g a)) ∧
    78        ∀ W', InUniv n W' → (∀ a, a ∈ˢ B → InFam W' (g a)) → x ∈ˢ Φ W' j

== whitepaper/Fragment/Access.lean#L80-L85
    80  /-- **Accessible operators are monotone**: the support in `W` is in
    81  the larger `W'`.  Con-leche: `AccTuple.monoTuple`. -/
    82  theorem AccFam.mono {n : Nat} {Φ : (ι → V) → ι → V} {A : V} (h : AccFam n Φ A) : MonoFam n Φ := by
    83    intro W W' hW hW' hle i x hx
    84    obtain ⟨B, g, -, hg, hs⟩ := h W hW i x hx
    85    exact hs W' hW' fun a ha => hle _ _ (hg a ha)

== whitepaper/Fragment/IndSem.lean#L1158-L1183
  1158  own supports `Bk` (by position). -/
  1159  noncomputable def instSupp (ps : List V) (c : CtorSpec) (fs : List V) (Bk : Nat → V) : V :=
  1160    listUnion ((List.range c.fields.length).map fun k =>
  1161      match c.fields[c.fields.length - 1 - k]? with
  1162      | some (.reflexive tele _) =>
  1163        image (pcons (nat k)) (ctxSet M (S.ψ ls) (consList (earlier fs k) (envP ps)) tele)
  1164      | some .container => image (pcons (nat k)) (Bk k)
  1165      | _ => empty)
  1166  
  1167  /-- The occurrence a code stands for: at a reflexive field, the field
  1168  at the code's position applied to the code's argument tuple, at the
  1169  field's index expressions there; at a container field, the container
  1170  value's own occurrence `gk` at the code, at the nested occurrence's
  1171  index expressions. -/
  1172  noncomputable def instOcc (ps : List V) (c : CtorSpec) (fs : List V) (gk : Nat → V → V) (b : V) :
  1173      List V × V :=
  1174    match c.fields[c.fields.length - 1 - idx (pfst b)]? with
  1175    | some (.reflexive _ es) =>
  1176      (S.idxVals M ls (consList (untuple (psnd b)) (consList (earlier fs (idx (pfst b))) (envP ps))) es,
  1177        appList (fieldVal fs (idx (pfst b))) (untuple (psnd b)).reverse)
  1178    | some .container =>
  1179      match S.nest with
  1180      | some N => (S.memberIdx M ls N ps, gk (idx (pfst b)) (psnd b))
  1181      | none => ([], pt)
  1182    | _ => ([], pt)

== whitepaper/Fragment/IndSem.lean#L1080-L1097
  1080  /-- **A constructor's support bound**: for each reflexive field, the
  1081  tuples of its telescope at every list fitting the fields before it
  1082  relative to the one-fibre family, each coded by the field's position
  1083  (a numeral in a path step, `pcons`); for each container field, the
  1084  class's bound, coded likewise.  An ordinary field contributes
  1085  nothing; a recursive field, whose telescope is empty, contributes the
  1086  one tuple `tuple []` per prefix.  Con-leche: `piBound` glued along the
  1087  telescope (`HoleAcc.lean`), made uniform along the fields
  1088  (`TeleAcc.lean`); the container's bound `accPaths` of
  1089  `ContAccFrame.lean`. -/

  1093      | some (.reflexive tele _) =>
  1094        famUnion (S.fitsSet M ls (S.oneFam ls) ps (c.fields.drop (c.fields.length - k))) fun t =>
  1095          image (pcons (nat k)) (ctxSet M (S.ψ ls) (consList (untuple t) (envP ps)) tele)
  1096      | some .container => image (pcons (nat k)) S.classBound
  1097      | _ => empty)

== whitepaper/Fragment/IndSem.lean#L601-L622
   601  /-- **The universe bound on the fields, at every family in the
   602  universe**: above a proposition, along any list fitting the fields
   603  before a position relative to a family of members of the result
   604  universe, an ordinary field's domain is a member of the result
   605  universe, and so is every entry of a reflexive field's telescope at
   606  every fitting prefix of the telescope.  Con-leche: the constructors'
   607  fields are small at every hole frame of the tuple space
   608  (`LfpClause.fieldsOk`, `ConLeche/Model/Env/BlockLfp.lean`, the
   609  install's `FieldsOkB`); the installation derives it from the checker's
   610  field-sort check read in a model in which the former denotes the
   611  one-fibre family (`domsBounded_of`, `InstallInd.lean`), whence every
   612  family by `domsBounded_of_fam`. -/
   613  def DomsBounded (ps : List V) : Prop :=
   614    S.z ls = false → ∀ W, InUniv (S.u₀ ls) W → ∀ c ∈ S.ctors, ∀ k f,
   615      c.fields[c.fields.length - 1 - k]? = some f → k < c.fields.length →
   616      ∀ fs, S.FitsFields M ls W ps (c.fields.drop (c.fields.length - k)) fs →
   617        match f with
   618        | .ordinary A => interp M (S.ψ ls) (consList fs (envP ps)) A ∈ˢ (univ (S.u₀ ls) : V)
   619        | .reflexive tele _ => ∀ t T, tele[t]? = some T → ∀ ys,
   620            FitsVals M (S.ψ ls) (consList fs (envP ps)) (tele.drop (t + 1)) ys →
   621            interp M (S.ψ ls) (consList ys (consList fs (envP ps))) T ∈ˢ (univ (S.u₀ ls) : V)
   622        | .container => True

   511  /-- **The operator is monotone**, from its accessibility (`AccW.mono`). -/
   512  theorem mono (h : LfpClause acval D) {ψ : Name → Nat} {ρp : Nat → V}

   514      MonoTuple (D.w ψ) D.N (D.idx ψ ρp) (D.Φ ψ ρp) :=
   515    (h.acc ψ ρp hsat).mono

== whitepaper/Fragment/Access.lean#L292-L303
   292  /-- **A closed family from accessibility.**  At a positive universe,
   293  an operator that maps families in the universe to families in the
   294  universe and is accessible with a bound `A` in the universe has a
   295  closed family in the universe: the limit family.  An element `Φ`
   296  produces from it has a support, each occurrence in some stage; the
   297  node whose subtree at `a` is a tree of the occurrence `g a`'s stage
   298  has that support in the union of its subtrees' stages, so its stage
   299  produces the element, which is therefore in the limit.  No
   300  monotonicity is used.  Con-leche: `closed_of_acc`,
   301  `ConLeche/SetModel/Access.lean`. -/
   302  theorem closed_of_acc (hn : n ≠ 0) (hA : A ∈ˢ (univ n : V)) (hmaps : MapsFam n Φ)
   303      (hacc : AccFam n Φ A) : ∃ L, IsClosedFam n Φ L := by

== whitepaper/Fragment/Access.lean#L163-L198
   163  /-- Lean-level well-founded trees branching over the sets: a leaf, or
   164  a node with a subtree for every set.  Con-leche: `BT`. -/
   165  inductive BT (V : Type u) : Type u
   166    | leaf : BT V
   167    | node : (V → BT V) → BT V
   168  
   169  namespace AccIter
   170  
   171  variable (Φ : (ι → V) → ι → V) (A : V)
   172  
   173  /-- The fibrewise union of an `A`-indexed family of families.
   174  Con-leche: `unionTup`. -/
   175  noncomputable def unionFam (F : V → ι → V) : ι → V := fun i => famUnion A fun a => F a i
   176  
   177  /-- **The stage at a tree**: the empty family at a leaf, `Φ` of the
   178  union of the subtrees' stages at a node.  Con-leche: `stage`. -/
   179  noncomputable def stage : BT V → ι → V
   180    | .leaf => fun _ => empty
   181    | .node f => Φ (unionFam A fun a => stage (f a))
   182  
   183  /-- **A tree's code**: its set of paths over `A` — the empty path at a
   184  node, and a step `a` onto every path of the subtree at `a`.
   185  Con-leche: `code`. -/
   186  noncomputable def code : BT V → V
   187    | .leaf => empty
   188    | .node f => binUnion one (famUnion A fun a => image (pcons a) (code (f a)))
   189  
   190  open Classical in
   191  /-- A tree with the given code, if any.  Con-leche: `pick`. -/
   192  noncomputable def pick (c : V) : BT V :=
   193    if h : ∃ T, code A T = c then Classical.choose h else .leaf
   194  
   195  /-- **The limit family**: the union of the stages over all codes.
   196  Con-leche: `limTup`. -/
   197  noncomputable def limFam : ι → V :=
   198    fun i => famUnion (power (accPaths A)) fun c => stage Φ A (pick A c) i

== whitepaper/Fragment/Access.lean#L304-L320
   304    refine ⟨limFam Φ A, limFam_mem hn hA hmaps, ?_⟩
   305    intro i x hx
   306    obtain ⟨B, g, hBA, hgL, hsupp⟩ := hacc _ (limFam_mem hn hA hmaps) i x hx
   307    -- every occurrence of the support lies in some stage: choose its tree
   308    have hT : ∀ a, a ∈ˢ B → ∃ T : BT V, (g a).2 ∈ˢ stage Φ A T (g a).1 :=
   309      fun a ha => mem_limFam.mp (hgL a ha)
   310    classical
   311    let f : V → BT V := fun a => if h : a ∈ˢ B then Classical.choose (hT a h) else .leaf
   312    have hstage : x ∈ˢ stage Φ A (.node f) i := by
   313      simp only [stage]
   314      refine hsupp _ (fun i' => famUnion_mem_univ hn hA fun a _ => stage_mem hn hA hmaps (f a) i') ?_
   315      intro a ha
   316      refine mem_unionFam.mpr ⟨a, hBA a ha, ?_⟩
   317      have : f a = Classical.choose (hT a ha) := dite_eq_left ha
   318      rw [this]
   319      exact Classical.choose_spec (hT a ha)
   320    exact mem_limFam.mpr ⟨_, hstage⟩

   185  Con-leche: `code`. -/
   186  noncomputable def code : BT V → V

== ConLeche/SetTheory/Derive/LfpTuple.lean#L78-L87
    78  /-- **The least pre-fixed tuple of `Φ`** — componentwise, fibrewise the
    79  intersection of the closed tuples when there is one (separated from a
    80  chosen closed tuple), dropped to `∅` if it left `strictU w`; the empty
    81  tuple otherwise. -/
    82  noncomputable def lfpTuple (w k : Nat) (Is : Nat → V) (Φ : (Nat → V) → Nat → V) : Nat → V :=
    83    fun m =>
    84      if h : ∃ L, IsClosedTuple w k Is Φ L then
    85        famOf (fun i => dropTo (strictU w) (sep (app (Classical.choose h m) i)
    86          (fun x => ∀ X, IsClosedTuple w k Is Φ X → x ∈ˢ app (X m) i))) (Is m)
    87      else famOf (fun _ => empty) (Is m)

== whitepaper/Fragment/IndRec.lean#L73-L81
    73  /-- **The operator** whose least fixed point is the recursor's graph:
    74  at the constructor value of fitting fields, the value is the
    75  constructor's minor at the fields and the inductive hypotheses.
    76  Con-leche: the graph functor `gStep` (`GraphRec.lean`). -/

    78    ∃ j c fs ihs, S.ctors[j]? = some c ∧ S.FitsFields M ls (S.Fam M ls ps) ps c.fields fs ∧
    79      is = S.idxVals M ls (consList fs (envP ps)) c.idx ∧ t = S.ctorVal ls j fs ∧
    80      ListRel (S.IhOk M ls R ps m mins fs) c.recFields ihs ∧
    81      v = appList (S.minorAt mins j) (fs.reverse ++ ihs)

== whitepaper/Fragment/IndLib.lean#L101-L104
   101  /-- **The least fixed point** of an operator on predicates: the
   102  intersection of every predicate closed under it. -/
   103  def Lfp {α : Sort _} (Φ : (α → Prop) → (α → Prop)) : α → Prop :=
   104    fun a => ∀ P : α → Prop, (∀ b, Φ P b → P b) → P a

== whitepaper/Fragment/Uniq.lean#L40-L50
    40  /-- **The subsingleton criterion, semantically**: at a proposition,
    41  at most one constructor, and every field of a fitting instance is
    42  the point (its domain is a proposition) or is read off the
    43  constructor's index expressions (the field's variable is one of
    44  them). -/
    45  def Subsingleton : Prop :=
    46    S.ctors.length ≤ 1 ∧
    47    ∀ c ∈ S.ctors, ∀ ps : List V, FitsVals M (S.ψ ls) base S.params ps → ∀ fs : List V,
    48      S.FitsFields M ls (S.Fam M ls ps) ps c.fields fs →
    49      ∀ k, k < c.fields.length →
    50        fieldVal fs k = pt ∨ Expr.bvar (c.fields.length - 1 - k) ∈ c.idx

== whitepaper/Fragment/IndRec.lean#L394-L408
   394  /-- **The recursor's set** at its own levels `lsr` (the elimination
   395  level in front, if large): the abstraction over its context — the
   396  parameters, the motive, the minors, the indices, the major — of the
   397  recursor's semantic value, the family read at the block's levels.
   398  Into `Prop` (`qv`) the body is the point outright: the motive's fibres
   399  are truth values, and the abstraction is read by its values,
   400  so a body that is not the point would make it a graph. -/

== whitepaper/Fragment/Rules.lean#L95-L174
    95    /-- **ι** (`Red.iota`, `Rel.lean:200`): a stored recursor applied to
    96    exactly its telescope — `numParams` parameters, `numMotives` motives,
    97    `numMinors` minor premises, `numIndices` indices and the major
    98    premise — whose major reduces to a constructor application with a
    99    rule, fires the rule: the rule's right-hand side, at the use's
   100    levels, applied to the parameters, motives and minors, then to the
   101    constructor's fields (its arguments after the parameters).  The rule
   102    is one of the block's own constructors' (no stored instantiation,
   103    `RecRule.inst`); an auxiliary recursor's rule fires by
   104    `Red.iotaNested`.
   105  
   106    The **certificates** are the fragment's form of `Rel.lean`'s `CertsF`
   107    and `piResidual` premises (`:227-236`).  The recursor's spine before the
   108    major needs none: a reduction claims nothing of a redex that is the
   109    point, and a redex that is not the point fits the recursor's telescope
   110    by the invariant's application slots (`teleFit_of_ne_pt`).  The reduced
   111    major's slot is certified — its type inferred and found definitionally
   112    equal to the domain the recursor's telescope leaves after the spine
   113    (`Expr.piResidual`) — and so is the constructor's argument spine against
   114    its stored type's `Π`-telescope (`Expr.piDomains`; the stored types have
   115    the spine's length of syntactic binders, `Expr.hasPis`).  Both are
   116    needed only where the major may denote the point (a family that may be a
   117    proposition): where the major's domain is strict, `iota_core_strict`
   118    (`Sound.lean`) needs neither; where the constructor's family is a
   119    proposition at every valuation, `Red.iotaProp` needs no slot
   120    certificate.  They make the environment's ι law (`EnvModel.lean`,
   121    `RecRuleLaw`) applicable: they put every argument in its domain.
   122  
   123    The **three comparisons** after them are `Rel.lean`'s too (`:213-241`,
   124    there in the certified case only): the constructor's levels are the
   125    recursor's (its last `usj.length` ones — a large eliminator carries
   126    one extra level in front), the constructor's parameters are
   127    definitionally the recursor's, and the constructor's residual type
   128    (`Expr.piResidual`: the family at the constructor's own parameters and
   129    index expressions, with the fields substituted in) has index
   130    expressions definitionally equal to the recursor's index arguments. In
   131    the model they matter exactly when the family is a proposition: there
   132    the major denotes the one point, the certificates say only that the
   133    fibre is inhabited, and the fields the rule's right-hand side receives
   134    can be related to the recursor's own parameters and indices through
   135    these comparisons alone (`Install.lean`). -/
   136    | iota {Γ : List Expr} {c : Name} {us : List Level} {ci : ConstInfo}
   137        {numParams numMotives numMinors numIndices : Nat} {rules : List RecRule}
   138        {args : List Expr} {major : Expr} {cj : Name} {usj : List Level}
   139        {cij : ConstInfo} {margs : List Expr} {rl : RecRule}
   140        {dM bM tM : Expr} {doms' tys' : List Expr}
   141        {residual : Expr} {I : Name} {lsI : List Level} {rps ridx : List Expr} :
   142        env.find? c = some ci →
   143        ci.kind = .recursor numParams numMotives numMinors numIndices rules →
   144        us.length = ci.lparams.length →
   145        args.length = numParams + numMotives + numMinors + numIndices + 1 →
   146        ci.type.hasPis (numParams + numMotives + numMinors + numIndices + 1) = true →
   147        Red env Γ (args.getD (numParams + numMotives + numMinors + numIndices) (bvar 0))
   148          major →
   149        major = mkAppN (const cj usj) margs →
   150        rl ∈ rules → rl.ctor = cj → rl.inst = none →
   151        env.find? cj = some cij →
   152        usj.length = cij.lparams.length →
   153        margs.length = numParams + rl.nfields →
   154        cij.type.hasPis (numParams + rl.nfields) = true →
   155        -- the major's slot certificate (the recursor's spine before it needs none)
   156        piResidual (ci.type.instL ci.lparams us)
   157          (args.take (numParams + numMotives + numMinors + numIndices)) = some (pi dM bM) →
   158        Infer env Γ major tM → DefEq env Γ tM dM →
   159        -- the constructor's telescope certificate
   160        piDomains (cij.type.instL cij.lparams usj) margs = some doms' →
   161        tys'.length = doms'.length →
   162        (∀ p ∈ margs.zip tys', Infer env Γ p.1 p.2) →
   163        (∀ p ∈ tys'.zip doms', DefEq env Γ p.1 p.2) →
   164        -- the constructor's levels, parameters and residual indices against the recursor's
   165        Level.eqList usj (us.drop (us.length - usj.length)) = true →
   166        (∀ p ∈ (margs.take numParams).zip (args.take numParams), DefEq env Γ p.1 p.2) →
   167        piResidual (cij.type.instL cij.lparams usj) margs = some residual →
   168        residual = mkAppN (const I lsI) (rps ++ ridx) →
   169        rps.length = numParams →
   170        (∀ p ∈ ridx.zip ((args.take (numParams + numMotives + numMinors + numIndices)).drop
   171          (numParams + numMotives + numMinors)), DefEq env Γ p.1 p.2) →
   172        Red env Γ (mkAppN (const c us) args)
   173          (mkAppN (rl.rhs.instL ci.lparams us)
   174            (args.take (numParams + numMotives + numMinors) ++ margs.drop numParams))

== ConLeche/Rules/Rel.lean#L186-L243
   186    /-- **ι** (`iotaRec`, `Kernel/Core.lean`): a stored recursor
   187    applied to exactly its telescope, whose prepared major (the `Red`
   188    premise: `prepareMajor`'s whnf / literal / rescue chain) is a
   189    constructor application with a firing rule.  The recursor
   190    telescope's syntactic arity over the redex's own spine, and (case 3
   191    only) the level and parameter comparisons with the rule's comparands,
   192    the constructor's full-grade telescope certificate and the index
   193    comparison are the checker's, in its order.
   194  
   195    **The ι case split** (task #342 L10, S5c): `iotaCase3` at the comparand
   196    levels is the checker's test.  A K rule, and a rule whose
   197    constructor's family is never `Prop` at the comparand levels (case 2),
   198    carry no premise about the constructor application; case 3 carries
   199    all four. -/
   200    | iota {d : Nat} {e : Expr} {c : Name} {us : List Level} {cv : ConstantVal}
   201        {mI rP : Nat} {rules : List RecRule} {major : Expr} {cj : Name}
   202        {usj : List Level} {cvj : ConstantVal} {cnP cnF : Nat} {rl : RecRule}
   203        {residual : Expr} :
   204        e.getAppFn = .const c us →
   205        env.find? c = some (.recInfo cv mI rP rules) →
   206        e.getAppArgs.length = mI + 1 →
   207        us.length = cv.levelParams.length →
   208        Red env d (e.getAppArgs.getD mI (.bvar 0)) major →
   209        major.getAppFn = .const cj usj →
   210        env.find? cj = some (.ctorInfo cvj cnP cnF) →
   211        rules.find? (fun r' => r'.ctor == cj) = some rl →
   212        major.getAppArgs.length = rl.ctorParams + rl.nfields →

   214            (recFireComparands rl cv.levelParams us cvj.levelParams
   215              e.getAppArgs rP).1 = true →
   216          Level.isEquivList usj
   217            (recFireComparands rl cv.levelParams us cvj.levelParams
   218              e.getAppArgs rP).1 = some true) →
   219        (iotaCase3 env.find? rl cvj
   220            (recFireComparands rl cv.levelParams us cvj.levelParams
   221              e.getAppArgs rP).1 = true →
   222          DefEqList env d (major.getAppArgs.take rl.ctorParams)
   223            (recFireComparands rl cv.levelParams us cvj.levelParams
   224              e.getAppArgs rP).2) →
   225        (Expr.peelPis e.getAppArgs.length
   226          (cv.type.instantiateLevelParams cv.levelParams us)).isSome = true →
   227        (iotaCase3 env.find? rl cvj
   228            (recFireComparands rl cv.levelParams us cvj.levelParams
   229              e.getAppArgs rP).1 = true →
   230          CertsF env d (cvj.type.instantiateLevelParams cvj.levelParams usj)
   231            major.getAppArgs) →
   232        (iotaCase3 env.find? rl cvj
   233            (recFireComparands rl cv.levelParams us cvj.levelParams
   234              e.getAppArgs rP).1 = true → mI ≠ rP →
   235          piResidual (cvj.type.instantiateLevelParams cvj.levelParams usj)
   236            major.getAppArgs = some residual) →
   237        (iotaCase3 env.find? rl cvj
   238            (recFireComparands rl cv.levelParams us cvj.levelParams
   239              e.getAppArgs rP).1 = true → mI ≠ rP →
   240          DefEqList env d (residual.getAppArgs.drop rl.ctorParams)
   241            ((e.getAppArgs.take mI).drop rP)) →
   242        Red env d e
   243          (Expr.mkAppN (rl.rhs.instantiateLevelParams cv.levelParams us)

== whitepaper/Fragment/Sound.lean#L821-L835
   821  /-- **A spine that is not the point fits its head's telescope, with no
   822  certificate** (the argument of the paper's ι rule, iterated).  At each step
   823  the application is not the point, so neither is its head
   824  (`app_pt`); the invariant's slot then puts the head in a function space
   825  (`piR false`), and the head's membership in its type — a function space, not
   826  the point — makes it a graph of that type's domain, so the slot's
   827  domain is the binder's (`piR_dom_unique`) and the argument lies in it.
   828  This is why `Red.iota` carries no certificate on the recursor's
   829  telescope: the reduction claims nothing of a redex that is the point. -/
   830  theorem teleFit_of_ne_pt {ρ : Nat → V} :
   831      ∀ {xs : List Expr} {f T : Expr},
   832        WellDenoted m.M φ ρ T → interp m.M φ ρ f ∈ˢ interp m.M φ ρ T →
   833        T.hasPis xs.length = true →
   834        WellDenoted m.M φ ρ (Expr.mkAppN f xs) → interp m.M φ ρ (Expr.mkAppN f xs) ≠ pt →
   835        TeleFit m.M φ ρ T xs

== ConLeche/Model/Env/Laws.lean#L521-L555
   521  /-- **The ι case split's environment facts, one rule**.
   522  `RecRuleLaw`'s main clause takes the levels, parameters and index
   523  comparisons as equations; under the conditional claims the ι step has
   524  them only where neither side is the point, and at a K rule or a family
   525  that is never `Prop` at the comparand levels it runs no check of the
   526  constructor application at all.  What the step consumes instead, at the
   527  recursor's levels:
   528  
   529  * **K** (`RecRule.k`): the rule's law at the recursor's own
   530    parameters, for any major value in the major's domain (the
   531    fragment's `RecRuleLawK`: inversion of the family's least
   532    fixed point) — the reduct, the minor, does not mention the major;
   533  * **the constructor's arity**: its stored type binds the spine
   534    syntactically, so a graded application of it that is not the point
   535    fits its telescope;
   536  * **(S) case 2**: where the family is never `Prop` at the comparand
   537    levels (`iotaCtorNeverProp`, the checker's test), the recursor's major
   538    domain holds no point;
   539  * **(T) case 2, the constructor's levels**: there a fired application
   540    that is not the point, at the constructor's own levels and spine, is
   541    also an application of the constructor at the comparand levels, to a
   542    graded spine with the same fields that fits its telescope there —
   543    the major's membership in the family at the comparands ties the
   544    injection's fields (the same argument as for the parameters), so the
   545    main law applies at the comparand levels;
   546  * **(P) the slot at the point**: where the major domain holds the
   547    point, every fitting constructor application is the point (the
   548    family is `Prop` there; the fragment's slot law);
   549  * **(U) coherence**: at a fired spine where the constructor application
   550    is the point (case 3, where the step compares the levels and
   551    parameters with the rule's comparands and the indices), the
   552    conditional index comparison is an equation (read off the
   553    parameters' conditional comparison).
   554  
   555  (P) and (U) are read only at case 3, so they take the level equation. -/

== whitepaper/Fragment/EnvModel.lean#L119-L186
   119  /-- **The ι law of one recursor rule** (con-leche's `RecRuleLaw`,
   120  `ConLeche/Model/Env/Laws.lean`), stated on **values**.  For the
   121  recursor `c` (stored as `ci`, with `numParams` parameters,
   122  `numBefore = numParams + numMotives + numMinors` arguments before the
   123  indices, the major at `majorIdx`) and its rule `rl` for the
   124  constructor stored as `cij`: whenever values `xs` up to the major,
   125  together with the constructor's set applied to values `ys` as the
   126  major, fit the recursor's telescope, `ys` fit the constructor's
   127  telescope, and the three comparisons of `Red.iota` hold in their
   128  semantic form — the constructor's levels evaluate as the recursor's
   129  last `usj.length` ones, its parameters equal the recursor's and the
   130  index expressions of its residual type (`piBodyV`: the family at the
   131  constructor's parameters and index expressions, read under the fields)
   132  denote the recursor's index arguments, **each where neither side is
   133  the point** (as `DefEq` claims them) — and the recursor's application
   134  is **not the point** (as `Red` claims ι), then the recursor's set
   135  applied to the spine is the rule's right-hand side's set applied to
   136  the parameters, motives, minors and the fields; and the right-hand
   137  side is well-denoted, with a well-formed application chain along
   138  those values (which is what makes the reduct well-denoted,
   139  `WellDenoted_mkAppN_of_spineOk`).
   140  
   141  Values rather than terms so that the law mentions the model only at
   142  the STORED terms (the two types and the right-hand side): extending
   143  the environment by a fresh constant then leaves every old law intact
   144  (`Install.lean`), where a law over arbitrary argument terms would have
   145  to be re-proved for the terms that mention the new name.  The ι rule's
   146  soundness converts its term-level certificates to this form
   147  (`Tele.lean`).
   148  
   149  **The installation's obligation, named.**  The conditional comparisons
   150  become the equalities the recursion equation needs because the
   151  recursor's and the constructor's telescopes are generated from one
   152  parameter and index context: under equal earlier values the two sides
   153  of each comparison lie in one type, whose members are all the point or
   154  none (`IsTy.eq_of_ne_pt`).  Where the family is a *type*, the law then
   155  follows from the **fixpoint's inversion**: the recursor's fit puts the
   156  major — a tagged tuple of the fields — in the family at the RECURSOR's
   157  parameters and indices, and a member of the family built by `rl.ctor`
   158  has its fields in the constructor's field telescope at THOSE
   159  parameters.  Where the family is a *proposition* the major denotes the
   160  point and the fits say only that the fibre is inhabited; the
   161  comparisons then relate the fields `ys` to the recursor's own
   162  parameters and indices, and the subsingleton criterion makes the
   163  recursor's value at the point the value at those fields. -/
   164  def RecRuleLaw (M : Name → List Nat → V) (c : Name) (ci : ConstInfo)
   165      (numParams numBefore majorIdx : Nat) (rl : RecRule) (cij : ConstInfo) : Prop :=
   166    ∀ (φ : Name → Nat) (ρ : Nat → V) (us usj : List Level) (xs ys : List V),
   167      us.length = ci.lparams.length → usj.length = cij.lparams.length →
   168      xs.length = majorIdx → ys.length = numParams + rl.nfields →
   169      TeleFitV M φ ρ (ci.type.instL ci.lparams us)
   170        (xs ++ [appList (M rl.ctor (usj.map (Level.eval φ))) ys]) →
   171      TeleFitV M φ ρ (cij.type.instL cij.lparams usj) ys →
   172      usj.map (Level.eval φ) = (us.drop (us.length - usj.length)).map (Level.eval φ) →
   173      (∀ p ∈ (ys.take numParams).zip (xs.take numParams), p.1 ≠ pt → p.2 ≠ pt → p.1 = p.2) →
   174      (∀ (B : Expr) (ρ' : Nat → V) (I : Name) (lsI : List Level) (rps ridx : List Expr),
   175        piBodyV ρ (cij.type.instL cij.lparams usj) ys = some (B, ρ') →
   176        B = Expr.mkAppN (.const I lsI) (rps ++ ridx) → rps.length = numParams →
   177        ∀ p ∈ (ridx.map (interp M φ ρ')).zip (xs.drop numBefore),
   178          p.1 ≠ pt → p.2 ≠ pt → p.1 = p.2) →
   179      appList (M c (us.map (Level.eval φ)))
   180          (xs ++ [appList (M rl.ctor (usj.map (Level.eval φ))) ys]) ≠ pt →
   181      appList (M c (us.map (Level.eval φ)))
   182          (xs ++ [appList (M rl.ctor (usj.map (Level.eval φ))) ys])
   183        = appList (interp M φ ρ (rl.rhs.instL ci.lparams us))
   184            (xs.take numBefore ++ ys.drop numParams) ∧
   185      WellDenoted M φ ρ (rl.rhs.instL ci.lparams us) ∧
   186      SpineOk (interp M φ ρ (rl.rhs.instL ci.lparams us)) (xs.take numBefore ++ ys.drop numParams)

== whitepaper/Fragment/Rules.lean#L394-L445
   394    /-- **ι, case 2** (the checker's ι case test): `Red.iota`
   395    with **no certificate at all** — no major slot, no constructor
   396    telescope — where the major's domain (what the recursor's telescope
   397    leaves after the spine, `Expr.piResidual`) is a stored inductive
   398    family applied to its parameters and indices whose stored sort is
   399    **never `Prop`** at the use: one level test, `1 ≤ u` at every
   400    valuation (`LevelOracle.le`, con-leche's `sortZ` read as `never`).
   401    The environment law `EnvModel.ind_fib` makes that domain strict,
   402    so a redex that is not the point has a major that is not the point;
   403    its reduction claim then applies, and the reduced constructor
   404    application fits the constructor's telescope with no certificate
   405    (`Sound.lean`, `iota_core_strict`).  The three comparisons are
   406    `Red.iota`'s, unchanged. -/
   407    | iotaStrict {Γ : List Expr} {c : Name} {us : List Level} {ci : ConstInfo}
   408        {numParams numMotives numMinors numIndices : Nat} {rules : List RecRule}
   409        {args : List Expr} {major : Expr} {cj : Name} {usj : List Level}

   414        env.find? c = some ci →

   416        us.length = ci.lparams.length →
   417        args.length = numParams + numMotives + numMinors + numIndices + 1 →
   418        ci.type.hasPis (numParams + numMotives + numMinors + numIndices + 1) = true →
   419        Red env Γ (args.getD (numParams + numMotives + numMinors + numIndices) (bvar 0))
   420          major →
   421        major = mkAppN (const cj usj) margs →
   422        rl ∈ rules → rl.ctor = cj → rl.inst = none →
   423        env.find? cj = some cij →

   427        -- case 2: the major's domain is a stored family whose sort is never `Prop` at the use
   428        piResidual (ci.type.instL ci.lparams us)

   430        dM = mkAppN (const I₀ ls₀) dargs →

   433        ci₀.type.hasPis (nP₀ + nI₀) = true →
   434        LevelOracle.le (.succ .zero) (S₀.sort.subst ci₀.lparams ls₀) = true →
   435        -- the constructor's levels, parameters and residual indices against the recursor's
   436        Level.eqList usj (us.drop (us.length - usj.length)) = true →
   437        (∀ p ∈ (margs.take numParams).zip (args.take numParams), DefEq env Γ p.1 p.2) →
   438        piResidual (cij.type.instL cij.lparams usj) margs = some residual →

   442          (numParams + numMotives + numMinors)), DefEq env Γ p.1 p.2) →

== whitepaper/Fragment/EnvModel.lean#L278-L296
   278  /-- **The fibres' regime follows the stored sort** (used by
   279  the ι case test): for a stored inductive type former
   280  `I` (stored as `ci`, with `nP` parameters and `nI` indices and its
   281  block's specification `S`), the family applied to any values fitting
   282  its telescope is a **truth value** where the family's stored sort
   283  `S.sort`, instantiated at the use's levels, evaluates to zero, and a
   284  **strict** set — not the point, and without the point as a member —
   285  where it does not (`Fib`).  Every `Sort (n+1)` holds truth values as
   286  well (`typeU`), so the universe does not say the second; the
   287  inductive model does: above a proposition a fibre is a set of tagged
   288  values (`IndSem.Fam_mem_typeU`), and a family read through a former's
   289  graph is admissible (`IndCommon.adm`), so strict
   290  (`IndCommon.strict_adm`).  Stated on values, like `RecRuleLaw`. -/
   291  def IndFibLaw (M : Name → List Nat → V) (I : Name) (ci : ConstInfo) (nP nI : Nat) (S : IndSpec) :
   292      Prop :=
   293    ∀ (φ : Name → Nat) (ρ : Nat → V) (ls : List Level) (vs : List V),
   294      ls.length = ci.lparams.length → vs.length = nP + nI →
   295      TeleFitV M φ ρ (ci.type.instL ci.lparams ls) vs →
   296      Fib (Level.eval φ (S.sort.subst ci.lparams ls) == 0) (appList (M I (ls.map (Level.eval φ))) vs)

== whitepaper/Fragment/Sound.lean#L1309-L1323
  1309  /-- **ι with no telescope certificate at all, where the major's domain
  1310  is strict** (the case of a family that is never a proposition).  If the
  1311  domain the major meets holds no point at the valuation — the case of an
  1312  inductive family whose sort is never `Prop` at the instance, whose
  1313  fibres are sets of tagged tuples — then a redex that is not the point
  1314  has a major that is not the point (the major lies in that domain,
  1315  `teleFit_of_ne_pt`), so the major's reduction claim applies; the
  1316  reduced major, a constructor application that is not the point, fits
  1317  the constructor's telescope by the same argument.  No certificate is
  1318  needed for the recursor's spine, the major or the constructor's
  1319  spine.  The strictness is a semantic hypothesis here (a sort above
  1320  `Prop` also holds truth values, so the universe does not give it);
  1321  `strict_dom` supplies it from the environment law
  1322  `EnvModel.ind_fib` and one level test (`Red.iotaStrict`). -/
  1323  theorem iota_core_strict {Γ : List Expr} {c : Name} {us : List Level} {ci : ConstInfo}

== whitepaper/Fragment/Rules.lean#L292-L347
   292    /-- **ι with no major-slot certificate and no level test** (the
   293    checker's certified case of ι).  `Red.iota`
   294    without the reduced major's slot certificate, for any family: the
   295    constructor's telescope certificate stays at the full grade (every
   296    parameter and field), and so do the three comparisons; nothing
   297    else is tested.  Why the slot needs nothing: where the unreduced
   298    major is not the point its reduction claim gives the reduct; where it
   299    is, the environment's slot law (`EnvModel.rec_rules_slot`) makes
   300    the constructor application the point too, given the redex is not
   301    (`Sound.lean`, `slot_of_law`, `iota_core_slot`).  On the generated
   302    recursors that law holds because the major's domain is the
   303    constructor's own family at the recursor's levels, a fibre holding the
   304    point is a truth value there, and the constructor of a family in
   305    `Prop` is the point (`IndSpec.rec_rule_slot`).  No premise links the
   306    major's domain to the constructor's family: the installation proves
   307    the slot law of every generated rule (`InstallIota.lean`).  This
   308    is the rule for a family that is a proposition at some valuations
   309    only (`Quot.{u}`, `PUnit.{u}`). -/

== whitepaper/Fragment/Sound.lean#L1003-L1012
  1003  /-- **A constructor of a family whose sort evaluates to zero denotes the
  1004  point**.  The
  1005  constructor applied to arguments that fit its stored type, whose
  1006  residual is the family `I` at some parameters and indices, at a level
  1007  where `I`'s sort evaluates to zero: the application lies in that
  1008  residual, a type of `Sort 0`, so it is the point
  1009  (`eq_pt_of_mem_sortZero`).  No argument of the application is read
  1010  beyond its fit: at such a level the constructor's arguments are not
  1011  constrained by its value. -/

== whitepaper/Fragment/EtaIota.lean#L681-L692
   681  /-- **The field counterexample, on values, and the eta path's answer to
   682  it**.  At a valuation where the structure is a
   683  proposition, the redex `rec minor (mk n)` with an ill-slotted field
   684  `n` is well-denoted and not the point.  Plain ι's reduct `minor n` is
   685  not well-denoted, so plain ι without a certificate on the field
   686  breaks the reduction claim; the eta reduct `minor (p0 (mk n))` is
   687  well-denoted and denotes what the redex does, so the step through the
   688  projections satisfies it with no certificate. -/

   691      ¬ RedSem (EnvModel.empty (witM (V := V))) φ [] redex1 plain1 ∧
   692      RedSem (EnvModel.empty (witM (V := V))) φ [] redex1 eta1 := by

== whitepaper/Fragment/EnvModel.lean#L250-L276
   250  /-- **The point in the major's slot** (the installer fact
   251  behind `Red.iotaSlot`/`Red.iotaNestedSlot`): for a recursor `c` and its
   252  rule `rl` firing on the constructor stored as `cij`, wherever the
   253  recursor's telescope holds the point as the major (after values `xs`
   254  fitting it), either the recursor's application there is the point or
   255  the rule's constructor, applied to anything, is — provided, for a rule
   256  of the block's own constructors (`rl.inst = none`), that the
   257  constructor's levels evaluate as the recursor's last ones (the level
   258  comparison ι runs).  On generated recursors: the major's domain is the
   259  family at the recursor's own levels; where its sort evaluates to zero
   260  the constructor (of the same family, at the same levels) is the point,
   261  and where it does not the domain is strict and holds no point.  On a
   262  nested block the family is `Prop` only where the eliminator is
   263  (`blockLargeElimAllowed`), so there the recursor's application is the
   264  point.  This is what lets the ι rules with no slot certificate go
   265  without a premise linking the major's domain to the constructor's
   266  family. -/
   267  def RecRuleSlotLaw (M : Name → List Nat → V) (c : Name) (ci : ConstInfo) (majorIdx : Nat)
   268      (rl : RecRule) (cij : ConstInfo) : Prop :=
   269    ∀ (φ : Name → Nat) (ρ : Nat → V) (us usj : List Level) (xs ys : List V),
   270      us.length = ci.lparams.length → usj.length = cij.lparams.length →
   271      xs.length = majorIdx →
   272      TeleFitV M φ ρ (ci.type.instL ci.lparams us) (xs ++ [pt]) →
   273      (rl.inst = none →
   274        usj.map (Level.eval φ) = (us.drop (us.length - usj.length)).map (Level.eval φ)) →
   275      appList (M c (us.map (Level.eval φ))) (xs ++ [pt]) = pt ∨
   276        appList (M rl.ctor (usj.map (Level.eval φ))) ys = pt

== whitepaper/Fragment/InstallIota.lean#L1046-L1056
  1046  /-- **The slot law of a generated rule** (`RecRuleSlotLaw`):
  1047  where the recursor's telescope holds the point as the major, the
  1048  fibre it lies in — the family at the recursor's own parameters,
  1049  indices and levels (`fits_recCtx_iff`) — holds the point, so the
  1050  family's sort is zero there (above it the fibre is a set of tagged
  1051  values, `mem_Fam_false`); the constructor, at levels that evaluate as
  1052  the recursor's (the level comparison), is then the point
  1053  (`ctorSet` at a proposition). -/
  1054  theorem rec_rule_slot {j : Nat} {c : CtorSpec} (hc : S.ctors[j]? = some c) :
  1055      RecRuleSlotLaw (S.M₃ m.M) S.recName S.recInfo (S.nP + 1 + S.n + S.nI)
  1056        ⟨c.name, c.fields.length, S.ruleRhs c j, none, S.isK⟩ (S.ctorInfo c) := by

== whitepaper/Fragment/Rules.lean#L493-L527
   493    /-- **ι by K** (Lean's
   494    `to_cnstr_when_K`): a recursor whose rule is flagged K
   495    (`RecRule.k`: one family, always a proposition, one constructor
   496    with no fields — `Eq`, `HEq`, `True`) reduces on its major **as it
   497    stands**, with no constructor in sight, to the rule's right-hand
   498    side at the recursor's parameters, motives and minors.  There is no
   499    certificate, no level, parameter or index comparison, and the major
   500    is not reduced.  What stays is K's **type check**, as in Lean: the
   501    major's inferred type reduces to a family application
   502    `I.{lsI} targs`, the constructor fabricated at its parameters
   503    `rl.ctor.{lsI} (targs.take numParams)` has a type `tF`, and
   504    `tF ≡ I.{lsI} targs`.  That check decides whether the step is taken
   505    (a verdict test); no claim consumes it.  Soundness is the
   506    environment's K law (`EnvModel.rec_rules_k`, proved in the
   507    installer by inversion of the least fixed point) with
   508    `Red.iotaK_core_sem`: a redex that is not the point fits the
   509    recursor's telescope, the major included, and the law needs nothing
   510    more. -/
   511    | iotaK {Γ : List Expr} {c : Name} {us : List Level} {ci : ConstInfo}
   512        {numParams numMotives numMinors numIndices : Nat} {rules : List RecRule}
   513        {args : List Expr} {rl : RecRule} {tM : Expr} {I : Name} {lsI : List Level}
   514        {targs : List Expr} {tF : Expr} :
   515        env.find? c = some ci →
   516        ci.kind = .recursor numParams numMotives numMinors numIndices rules →
   517        us.length = ci.lparams.length →
   518        args.length = numParams + numMotives + numMinors + numIndices + 1 →
   519        ci.type.hasPis (numParams + numMotives + numMinors + numIndices + 1) = true →
   520        rl ∈ rules → rl.k = true →
   521        -- K's type check on the major as it stands (a verdict test, consumed by no claim)
   522        Infer env Γ (args.getD (numParams + numMotives + numMinors + numIndices) (bvar 0)) tM →
   523        Red env Γ tM (mkAppN (const I lsI) targs) →
   524        Infer env Γ (mkAppN (const rl.ctor lsI) (targs.take numParams)) tF →
   525        DefEq env Γ tF (mkAppN (const I lsI) targs) →
   526        Red env Γ (mkAppN (const c us) args)
   527          (mkAppN (rl.rhs.instL ci.lparams us) (args.take (numParams + numMotives + numMinors)))

== whitepaper/Fragment/EnvModel.lean#L188-L214
   188  /-- **The ι law of a K rule** (the `EnvModel` field
   189  `rec_rules_k`, proved by the installer as
   190  `IndSpec.rec_rule_lawK`).
   191  For a recursor `c` whose one rule `rl` fires on a constructor with no
   192  fields of a family of sort `Prop` (Lean's K: `Eq`, `HEq`, `True`): at
   193  **any** values `vs` fitting the recursor's whole telescope — the
   194  major's value included, whatever term produced it — an application
   195  that is not the point equals the rule's right-hand side applied to the
   196  parameters, motives and minors alone.  In the inductive model this is
   197  the plain law at the recursor's own parameters plus **inversion of the
   198  least fixed point**: the major's value lies in the fibre at the
   199  recursor's indices, a fibre is inhabited only at the indices of the
   200  unique constructor applied to those parameters (the family "inhabited
   201  exactly there" is closed under the constructor, so it contains the
   202  least one), and the constructor's value there is the point, as the
   203  major's is.  The constructor application the checker fabricates (or
   204  finds) is not mentioned: the reduct does not contain it. -/
   205  def RecRuleLawK (M : Name → List Nat → V) (c : Name) (ci : ConstInfo)
   206      (numBefore majorIdx : Nat) (rl : RecRule) : Prop :=
   207    ∀ (φ : Name → Nat) (ρ : Nat → V) (us : List Level) (vs : List V),
   208      us.length = ci.lparams.length → vs.length = majorIdx + 1 →
   209      TeleFitV M φ ρ (ci.type.instL ci.lparams us) vs →
   210      appList (M c (us.map (Level.eval φ))) vs ≠ pt →
   211      appList (M c (us.map (Level.eval φ))) vs
   212          = appList (interp M φ ρ (rl.rhs.instL ci.lparams us)) (vs.take numBefore) ∧
   213        WellDenoted M φ ρ (rl.rhs.instL ci.lparams us) ∧
   214        SpineOk (interp M φ ρ (rl.rhs.instL ci.lparams us)) (vs.take numBefore)

== whitepaper/Fragment/InstallIota.lean#L981-L1002
   981  /-- **The K law of a generated rule** (`RecRuleLawK`):
   982  for a block with one constructor `c`, which has no fields, at ANY
   983  values fitting the recursor's telescope — the major's value whatever
   984  term produced it — the recursor is the rule's right-hand side at the
   985  parameters, motive and minor alone.  The proof is **inversion of the
   986  least fixed point**: the recursor's fit puts the major's value `t` in
   987  the fibre at the recursor's own parameters and indices
   988  (`fits_recCtx_iff`), and a member of a fibre is a constructor instance
   989  over the family (`IndSpec.mem_Fam`, the fixed-point equation); with
   990  one constructor and no fields that instance is `c` at the recursor's
   991  parameters, its index values are the indices, and `t` is its value
   992  (at a proposition the point, above it the empty tagged tuple).  The
   993  plain law's second half (`rec_rule_core`) then applies at the
   994  recursor's own parameters.  So the constructor's parameter telescope
   995  needs no comparison with the recursor's: the inversion is read off the
   996  recursor's fit, in the block's own parameter context.  Neither the
   997  family's sort nor the elimination level is used: the law holds for
   998  every one-constructor, fieldless block (Lean's K adds "is `Prop`",
   999  `isK`, and so does the flag). -/
  1000  theorem rec_rule_lawK {c : CtorSpec} (hK : S.ctors = [c]) (hnf : c.fields = []) :
  1001      RecRuleLawK (S.M₃ m.M) S.recName S.recInfo (S.nP + 1 + S.n) (S.nP + 1 + S.n + S.nI)
  1002        ⟨c.name, c.fields.length, S.ruleRhs c 0, none, S.isK⟩ := by

== ConLeche/Kernel/CoreDefs.lean#L85-L93
    85  def iotaCtorNeverProp (find? : Name → Option ConstantInfo) (cvj : ConstantVal)
    86      (us : List Level) : Bool :=
    87    match (cvj.type.piResult).getAppFn with
    88    | .const T _ =>
    89      match find? T with
    90      | some (.indInfo cvT caps) =>
    91        cvT.levelParams.length == us.length && capsNeverZero cvT.levelParams us caps
    92      | _ => false
    93    | _ => false

== whitepaper/Fragment/Consistency.lean#L36-L50
    36  
    37  /-- **The environments the checker accepts**: the empty environment,
    38  a definition the definition check passes, an inductive block the
    39  block check passes, a theorem the theorem check passes (con-leche's
    40  `addDecl`, `ConLeche/Kernel/Env.lean`, run to completion). -/
    41  inductive Accepted : Env → Prop
    42    /-- Nothing is stored. -/
    43    | empty : Accepted Env.empty
    44    /-- A definition (`DefOk`, `Decl.lean`). -/
    45    | defn {env : Env} {c : Name} {ci : ConstInfo} :
    46        Accepted env → DefOk env c ci → Accepted (env.add c ci)
    47    /-- An inductive block, plain or nested (`IndOk`, `Decl.lean`). -/

    49    /-- A theorem (`ThmOk`, `Decl.lean`), stored as its statement. -/
    50    | thm {env : Env} {c : Name} {ci : ConstInfo} {v : Expr} :

== whitepaper/Fragment/Consistency.lean#L54-L59
    54  /-- An accepted environment is closed: its stored terms mention only
    55  stored constants, at their own level parameters. -/
    56  theorem Accepted.scoped : ∀ {env : Env}, Accepted env → Env.Scoped env
    57    | _, .empty => Env.Scoped.empty
    58    | _, .defn h hok => h.scoped.add_def hok
    59    | _, .ind S h hok => h.scoped.install_any hok

== whitepaper/Fragment/Consistency.lean#L62-L79
    62  /-- **Every accepted environment has a model** (in any `IndLib`) — a
    63  block model, which remembers its blocks for the nestings to come
    64  (`BlockModel.lean`). -/
    65  theorem accepted_model {env : Env} (h : Accepted env) : Nonempty (BlockModel V env) := by
    66    induction h with
    67    | empty => exact ⟨BlockModel.empty fun _ _ => pt⟩
    68    | defn h hok ih =>
    69      obtain ⟨m⟩ := ih
    70      obtain ⟨m', -, -⟩ := install_def' h.scoped m hok
    71      exact ⟨m'⟩
    72    | ind S h hok ih =>
    73      obtain ⟨m⟩ := ih
    74      obtain ⟨m', -⟩ := install_ind_any h.scoped m hok
    75      exact ⟨m'⟩
    76    | thm h hok ih =>
    77      obtain ⟨m⟩ := ih
    78      obtain ⟨m', -, -⟩ := install_thm h.scoped m hok
    79      exact ⟨m'⟩

== ConLeche/Kernel/Inductives/Positivity.lean#L1453-L1496
  1453  def nestPos (ops : CheckerOps m) (env : Env) (ctx : NestCtx) :
  1454      Nat → List NestHole → Nat → Nat → Expr → NestState → m (NestFieldKind × Expr × NestState)
  1455    | 0, _, _, _, _, _ => throw (.notImplemented "nested positivity: fuel")
  1456    | fuel + 1, prog, dep, kb, e, st => do
  1457      let hi := ctx.hiAt prog.length
  1458      let w ← ops.whnf env dep e
  1459      -- `const`: the reduct mentions no member and no hole; the normal
  1460      -- form is the input when it mentions none either, else the reduct
  1461      if !w.nestOcc ctx.names ctx.nP hi then
  1462        return (.ordinary, (if e.nestOcc ctx.names ctx.nP hi then w else e), st)
  1463      match w with
  1464      | .forallE a b =>
  1465        -- `pi`: the domain hole-free, the codomain positive
  1466        if a.nestOcc ctx.names ctx.nP hi then
  1467          throw (.invalid "nested positivity: non positive occurrence of the datatypes \
  1468            being declared")
  1469        let (k, nb, st) ←
  1470          nestPos ops env ctx fuel prog (dep + 1) (kb + 1) (b.instantiate1 (.fvar dep a)) st
  1471        pure (k, .forallE a (nb.abstract1 dep), st)
  1472      | _ =>
  1473        let args := w.getAppArgs
  1474        match w.getAppFn with
  1475        | .fvar i _ =>
  1476          -- `holeApp`: a hole (`nestHoleAt`) — a member's, the ROOT frame's,
  1477          -- or a container frame's, its instantiation in progress — standing
  1478          -- for its entry's whole application to the parameters, applied to
  1479          -- hole-free indices, at its full arity (official
  1480          -- `is_valid_ind_app`, :338–341)
  1481          match nestHoleAt ctx prog i with
  1482          | some h =>
  1483            if args.all (fun x => !x.nestOcc ctx.names ctx.nP hi) &&
  1484                args.length + h.key.ds.length == nestArity ctx h.key.cname then
  1485              return (if i < ctx.hiAt 0 then
  1486                  (if kb == 0 then .recursive (i - ctx.nP) else .reflexive (i - ctx.nP))
  1487                else .inProgress, w, st)
  1488            else throw nestNonValid
  1489          | none => throw nestNonValid
  1490        | .const n us =>
  1491          -- a member constant left after the abstraction (other levels)
  1492          if ctx.names.contains n then throw nestNonValid
  1493          -- `contApp`: a stored inductive at a concrete instantiation
  1494          let (k, st) ← nestCont ctx ops env (nestPos ops env ctx fuel) prog kb n us args st
  1495          pure (k, w, st)
  1496        | _ => throw nestNonValid

== ConLeche/Kernel/Inductives/Positivity.lean#L1554-L1568
  1554  def nestUniformOk (ctx : NestCtx) (cv : ConstantVal) : Bool :=
  1555    !cv.type.piDomsOcc ctx.names ctx.nP (ctx.hiAt 0) ctx.nP &&
  1556      match nestRootCanon ctx cv with
  1557      | some crest => !crest.nestOcc ctx.names 0 0
  1558      | none => false
  1559  
  1560  /-- `nestUniformOk` at every stored constructor of every member, before
  1561  the walk (official runs it before anything else): a REJECT with
  1562  official's wording. -/
  1563  def nestUniform (ctx : NestCtx) (ctorss : List (List (ConstantVal × Nat))) : m Unit :=
  1564    match ctorss.findSome? (·.find? (!nestUniformOk ctx ·.1)) with
  1565    | some c => throw (.invalid s!"invalid occurrence of a datatype being declared in the \
  1566        type of {c.1.name}: it must be applied to the parameters and universe levels of the \
  1567        mutual declaration")
  1568    | none => pure ()

== ConLeche/Kernel/Inductives/Positivity.lean#L1110-L1116
  1110  /-- **A stored constructor type at a key** (see the section header): its
  1111  canonical abstraction (`nestCanonCrest`, the group `names` at the key's
  1112  levels `us`), then the key's parameters `ds` and the frame's holes
  1113  `holes` (one per member of `names`, in order) put in. -/
  1114  def nestCrest (names : List Name) (us : List Level) (ds holes : List Expr) (cty : Expr) :
  1115      Option Expr :=
  1116    (nestCanonCrest names us ds.length cty).map (·.replaceFVars (nestKeyMap ds holes))

  1476          -- `holeApp`: a hole (`nestHoleAt`) — a member's, the ROOT frame's,
  1477          -- or a container frame's, its instantiation in progress — standing
  1478          -- for its entry's whole application to the parameters, applied to

  1487                else .inProgress, w, st)

== ConLeche/Kernel/Inductives/Positivity.lean#L1415-L1440
  1415  def nestCont (ctx : NestCtx) (ops : CheckerOps m) (env : Env)
  1416      (rec : List NestHole → Nat → Nat → Expr → NestState → m (NestFieldKind × Expr × NestState))
  1417      (prog : List NestHole) (kb : Nat) (n : Name) (us : List Level) (args : List Expr)
  1418      (st : NestState) : m (NestFieldKind × NestState) := do
  1419    let q ← unwrapOr (nestContainer ctx n) nestNonValid
  1420    if args.length < q.1 ||
  1421        !(args.drop q.1).all (fun x => !x.nestOcc ctx.names ctx.nP (ctx.hiAt prog.length)) then
  1422      throw nestNonValid
  1423    -- `Quot` is stored as an `.indInfo` but is no inductive for
  1424    -- official (`is_nested_inductive_app` asks `is_inductive()`):
  1425    -- the one name read here.  Every other basis type (`Eq`, `Nat`,
  1426    -- `Empty`, `False`, and `And`) is a container like any stored
  1427    -- inductive.
  1428    if n == quotName then throw nestNonValid
  1429    unless (args.take q.1).all (fun x => x.bvarB == 0 && x.fvarB ≤ ctx.hiAt prog.length) do
  1430      throw (.invalid "nested positivity: nested inductive datatypes parameters \
  1431        cannot contain local variables")
  1432    -- the instance is FULLY applied: the container case
  1433    -- compares the container's family at the index tuple, and a partial
  1434    -- application is a function, whose graph does not grow with its values.
  1435    -- A field's domain is a type, so a checked constructor never has one.
  1436    let ni ← nestInstType ctx (ctx.hiAt prog.length) ⟨n, us, args.take q.1⟩
  1437    unless args.length == q.1 + ni.1 do
  1438      throw (.invalid "nested positivity: type expected (a container instance that is not \
  1439        fully applied)")
  1440    nestContKey ctx ops env rec prog kb n us (args.take q.1) q.1 ni.2 st

== ConLeche/Kernel/Inductives/Positivity.lean#L1124-L1158
  1124  def nestInstType (ctx : NestCtx) (hi : Nat) (key : NestKey) : m (Nat × Expr) := do
  1125    let cvC ← unwrapOr (match ctx.find? key.cname with
  1126        | some (.indInfo cv _) => some cv
  1127        | _ => none)
  1128      (.internal "nested positivity: container vanished")
  1129    -- the container is applied at its own level count (official:
  1130    -- `infer_constant`'s "incorrect number of universe levels", which every
  1131    -- constant of a checked constructor type — and of every
  1132    -- reduct of it — passed; the model reads the key's constants at it)
  1133    unless key.lvls.length = cvC.levelParams.length do
  1134      throw (.invalid "nested positivity: incorrect number of universe levels for a nested \
  1135        inductive datatype (official: incorrect number of universe levels)")
  1136    -- the container's parameters are a SYNTACTIC telescope (its canonical
  1137    -- instantiation exists, so the N2 check below reads
  1138    -- against the container's recorded index telescope; every stored
  1139    -- inductive's parameters are binders of its type, as official checks)
  1140    unless (cvC.type.stripPis key.ds.length).isSome do
  1141      throw (.invalid "nested positivity: invalid nested inductive datatype, its type does \
  1142        not bind its parameters (official: ill-formed inductive type)")
  1143    let ty ← unwrapOr (instPisWith key.ds
  1144        (cvC.type.instantiateLevelParams cvC.levelParams key.lvls))
  1145      (.invalid "nested positivity: invalid nested inductive datatype, its type does not bind \
  1146        its parameters (official: ill-formed inductive type)")
  1147    let s ← unwrapOr (match ty.piBinders.2 with
  1148        | .sort s => some s
  1149        | _ => none)
  1150      (.invalid "nested positivity: invalid nested inductive datatype, its type is not a \
  1151        telescope ending in a sort (official: type expected)")
  1152    if ty.piBinders.1.any (fun b => b.nestOcc ctx.names ctx.nP hi) then
  1153      throw (.invalid "nested positivity: a container's index telescope mentions the block \
  1154        (official: unknown constant)")
  1155    unless ← liftFueled "level comparison" (Level.isEquiv s ctx.sort) do
  1156      throw (.invalid "nested positivity: mutually inductive types must live in the \
  1157        same universe")
  1158    pure (ty.piBinders.1.length, ty)

== ConLeche/Kernel/Inductives/Positivity.lean#L1333-L1351
  1333  def nestFrame (ctx : NestCtx) (ops : CheckerOps m) (env : Env)
  1334      (rec : List NestHole → Nat → Nat → Expr → NestState → m (NestFieldKind × Expr × NestState))
  1335      (prog : List NestHole) (hi : Nat) (us : List Level) (ds : List Expr) (nPc : Nat)
  1336      (grp : List (Name × Expr)) (st : NestState) : m NestState := do
  1337    -- K.52: the instantiation `C.{us} ds` is TYPED at the
  1338    -- frame's own depth (its holes typed by their containers' formers, as
  1339    -- the constants they stand for).  Official imposes it: after the nested
  1340    -- elimination, `add_inductive` type-checks every replaced nested
  1341    -- application `I Ds` (`tc.check(nested, …)` over `m_aux2nested`,
  1342    -- `inductive.cpp` v4.32.2 :1186–1189, v4.34.0 :1320–1323), and a reduct
  1343    -- of a typed term is typed.  The model grades the key's parameters in
  1344    -- the frame's stack context by it.
  1345    let _ ← ops.inferType env hi (Expr.mkAppN (.const (grp.headD default).1 us) ds)
  1346    let prog' := (grp.mapIdx fun _ (c, _) =>
  1347      ({ key := ⟨c, us, ds⟩, base := hi } : NestHole)).reverse ++ prog
  1348    let ctors ← nestGroupCtors ctx nPc (grp.map (·.1))
  1349    let (_, st) ← nestCtors ctx ops env (fun _ => rec) prog' (hi + grp.length) us ds (grp.map (·.1))
  1350      (grp.mapIdx fun i (_, ty) => Expr.fvar (hi + i) ty) ctors st
  1351    pure st

== ConLeche/Kernel/Inductives/Positivity.lean#L1213-L1262
  1213  def nestCtors (ctx : NestCtx) (ops : CheckerOps m) (env : Env)
  1214      (rec : Expr → List NestHole → Nat → Nat → Expr → NestState →
  1215        m (NestFieldKind × Expr × NestState))
  1216      (prog : List NestHole) (hi : Nat) (us : List Level) (ds : List Expr) (names : List Name)
  1217      (holes : List Expr) :
  1218      List (ConstantVal × Nat) → NestState → m (List (List NestFieldKind × Expr) × NestState)
  1219    | [], st => pure ([], st)
  1220    | (cv, nF) :: cs, st => do
  1221      -- the constructor's level parameters are distinct (the substitution law
  1222      -- instantiates them as the recorded reading does;
  1223      -- every stored constant passed `checkConstantVal`'s own check)
  1224      unless Name.nodup cv.levelParams do
  1225        throw (.invalid "nested positivity: invalid nested inductive datatype, its constructor \
  1226          has a duplicate universe level parameter (official: duplicate universe level \
  1227          parameter)")
  1228      -- the container's constructor at the key, its group's WHOLE
  1229      -- applications replaced by the holes BEFORE its parameters are
  1230      -- instantiated (`nestCrest`), WITHOUT a β-step (official's
  1231      -- `instantiate_pi_params`, `inductive.cpp` v4.34.0)
  1232      let crest ← unwrapOr
  1233        (nestCrest names us ds holes (cv.type.instantiateLevelParams cv.levelParams us))
  1234        (.invalid "nested positivity: invalid nested inductive datatype, its constructor type \
  1235          does not bind the parameters (official: ill-formed constructor)")
  1236      let ty ← ops.inferType env hi crest
  1237      let _ ← ops.ensureSort env hi ty
  1238      let (ks, nds, cur, st) ← nestFields (rec crest) prog hi
  1239        (.invalid "nested positivity: invalid nested inductive datatype, its constructor type \
  1240          does not bind its fields (official: ill-formed constructor)") nF 0 crest st
  1241      -- U4 on the instantiated constructor: no later field and not the result
  1242      -- reads a field that is
  1243      -- not ordinary (recursive, reflexive, nested or in progress) — on the
  1244      -- walked (whnf'd) telescope.  Official rejects every instance
  1245      -- (charter item 9)
  1246      if (List.range nF).any (fun i => ks.getD i .ordinary != .ordinary &&
  1247          structUsedLater (closeTelescope nds hi cur) 0 i) then
  1248        throw (.invalid "nested positivity: non valid occurrence of the datatypes being \
  1249          declared (a later field or the result depends on a recursive or nested field)")
  1250      -- official's "invalid return type" on the instantiated constructor; its
  1251      -- result is headed by its hole, applied to its indices alone (never
  1252      -- fires: a stored constructor's result is its inductive applied to
  1253      -- the parameters, which `nestCrest` abstracts)
  1254      unless nestResHead cur && cur.getAppArgs.all
  1255          (fun x => !x.nestOcc ctx.names ctx.nP hi) do
  1256        throw (.invalid "nested positivity: invalid return type — a constructor's result \
  1257          index mentions the block")
  1258      -- K.53′: the constructor's walked normal form at the
  1259      -- frame's key, read back (`NestCtorNf`)
  1260      let st := { st with ctorNfs := st.ctorNfs.push (nestCtorNf ctx prog hi us ds cv nds cur) }
  1261      let (os, st) ← nestCtors ctx ops env rec prog hi us ds names holes cs st
  1262      pure ((ks, closeTelescope nds hi cur) :: os, st)

== ConLeche/Kernel/Inductives/Positivity.lean#L1591-L1599

  1592      List (List (ConstantVal × Nat)) → NestState →
  1593        m (List (List (List NestFieldKind × Expr)) × NestState)
  1594    | [], st => pure ([], st)
  1595    | cs :: css, st => do
  1596      let (o, st) ← nestCtors ctx ops env (fun crest => nestPos ops env ctx (whnfWalkFuel crest)) []
  1597        (ctx.hiAt 0) (ctx.lps.map .param) ctx.params ctx.names holes cs st
  1598      let (os, st) ← nestRoot ops env ctx holes css st
  1599      pure (o :: os, st)

== ConLeche/Kernel/Inductives/GenRec.lean#L138-L158
   138  /-- Constructor `x`'s minor premise type at depth `d`, of class `c`: its
   139  declared fields, then per recursive field `f` (walked type `w`) the
   140  inductive hypothesis `∀ a⃗, motive_t e⃗ (f a⃗)`, over the motive at the
   141  declared result indices and the constructor applied. -/
   142  def ClassGen.minorTy (g : ClassGen) (c : Nat) (x : ClassCtor) (d : Nat) : Option Expr := do
   143    let ci := g.cls.getD c default
   144    let (fvs, res) ← openPisAtFvars x.nF x.tyD d
   145    let ws ← targetPiDomsWith fvs x.tyN
   146    let recs := (List.range x.nF).filterMap fun i =>
   147      match x.kinds.getD i .ordinary with
   148      | .recursive t tele => some (i, t, tele)
   149      | .ordinary => none
   150    let ihs ← (List.range recs.length).mapM fun l => do
   151      let (i, t, tele) := recs.getD l default
   152      let e := d + x.nF + l
   153      let (xs, idx) ← g.ihParts t tele (ws.getD i default) e
   154      pure (closeTelescope (xs.map g.binder) e
   155        (Expr.mkAppN (g.motVar t) (idx ++ [Expr.mkAppN (fvs.getD i default) xs])))
   156    let concl := Expr.mkAppN (g.motVar c)
   157      (res.getAppArgs.drop ci.nPc ++ [Expr.mkAppN (.const x.cv.name ci.lvls) (ci.ds ++ fvs)])
   158    pure (closeTelescope (fvs.map g.binder ++ ihs) d concl)

== ConLeche/Kernel/Inductives/GenRec.lean#L175-L182
   175  /-- **The generated recursor type** at class `c`. -/
   176  def classGenRecTy (g : ClassGen) (c : Nat) : Option Expr := do
   177    let pre := g.pre
   178    let rP := pre.length
   179    let (ifs, maj) ← g.major c rP
   180    let t : Expr := .fvar (rP + ifs.length) maj
   181    pure (closeTelescope (pre ++ ifs.map g.binder ++ [maj]) 0
   182      (Expr.mkAppN (g.motVar c) (ifs ++ [t])))

== ConLeche/Kernel/Inductives/GenRec.lean#L184-L207
   184  /-- **The generated rule** of a recursor at class `c` for its constructor
   185  `x`: `λ p⃗ (prefix) f⃗, minor f⃗ (λ a⃗, rec_t p⃗ (prefix) e⃗ (f a⃗))…`, the
   186  callee `rec_t` the family's recursor at the landing class `t`
   187  (`recOf`). -/
   188  def classGenRule (g : ClassGen) (recOf : Nat → Option Name) (rlvls : List Level) (c : Nat)
   189      (x : ClassCtor) : Option Expr := do
   190    let pre := g.pre
   191    let rP := pre.length
   192    let (s, _) ← (List.range g.slots.length).zip g.slots |>.find? fun (_, sl) =>
   193      match sl with | .minor c' C _ => c' == c && C == x.cv.name | _ => false
   194    let (fvs, _) ← openPisAtFvars x.nF x.tyD rP
   195    let ws ← targetPiDomsWith fvs x.tyN
   196    let pvars := (List.range rP).map fun i => if i < g.nP then g.params.getD i default else
   197      g.slotVar (i - g.nP)
   198    let ihs ← (List.range x.nF).filterMapM fun i =>
   199      match x.kinds.getD i .ordinary with
   200      | .ordinary => some none
   201      | .recursive t tele => do
   202        let f := fvs.getD i default
   203        let (xs, idx) ← g.ihParts t tele (ws.getD i default) (rP + x.nF)
   204        let r ← recOf t
   205        pure (some (closeLams (xs.map g.binder) (rP + x.nF)
   206          (Expr.mkAppN (.const r rlvls) (pvars ++ idx ++ [Expr.mkAppN f xs]))))
   207    pure (closeLams (pre ++ fvs.map g.binder) 0 (Expr.mkAppN (g.slotVar s) (fvs ++ ihs)))

    15  * the CLASSES — the types the family eliminates, one per MOTIVE of the

== ConLeche/Model/Inductives/ContAcc.lean#L15-L34
    15  /-!
    16  # A container instance is accessible
    17  
    18  The container pieces of the accessibility induction on the positivity
    19  derivation (`posD_acc`, `PosDerivAcc.lean`):
    20  
    21  * the leaf (`accConcl_of_frameAccOut`, over `keyLeaf`): a frame's
    22    accessibility at the key frames makes the container instance
    23    accessible along the enclosing relation;
    24  * a frame's accessibility at EMPTY enclosing frames, read back at the
    25    frameless relation (`frameAccOut_unextend`, with
    26    `HoleRelA.extendEmpty`);
    27  * a key accessible at the block's own depth (`KeyAcc`) makes a cache
    28    hit's instance accessible (`contHit_acc`, at the enclosing relation
    29    seen at that depth, `HoleRelA.dropBase`).
    30  
    31  The TYPE REGIME of a container instance: the container lives at the
    32  block's level (`n2_sort`, the kernel's N3), so a truth-valued fibre of a
    33  container is empty (`LfpClause.injNePt`).
    34  -/

   530  /-- **THE NESTED CASE: the least tuple is accessible in its parameter.**
   531  If the joint operator `Θ` (parameter components first, then its own) is

== ConLeche/SetModel/NestRec.lean#L8-L46
     8  /-!
     9  # The nested recursor's graph kit: majors over several CLASSES
    10  
    11  The graph kit (`SetModel/GraphRec.lean`, `GraphRecKit`) asks ONE thing of
    12  the majors: an induction principle (`ind`).  At a flat block the majors
    13  are the members' carriers and `ind` is the block's lfp induction.  At a
    14  NESTED block the recursor family also ranges over the CONTAINER CLASSES
    15  — `List Tree`, `Rose T`, `List (Rose T)` — each the least fixed point of
    16  its OWN operator, at its OWN instantiation (the container's lfp clause at
    17  the parameter frame the instantiation reads).  This module builds the
    18  kit over such a family of classes and proves `ind` from the classes'
    19  own clauses, by a STRENGTHENED PREDICATE:
    20  
    21  * a class is a clause (`SClause`: an operator per parameter frame, its
    22    fit relation and injections) at its TRUE frame `fr b`;
    23  * its container fields' classes are reached, during the induction, at
    24    SEPARATED frames — the instantiation read at the enclosing class's
    25    separated tuple; which frames count is the kit's `Adm` (admissible:
    26    "a frame whose parameter positions hold elements satisfying `G`");
    27  * at such a frame the class's own induction runs with the predicate
    28    "lies in the TRUE class ∧ the property"; membership in the true class
    29    is re-established at each constructor by the class's clause at the
    30    TRUE frame (the fibre law, backwards, and closure), after moving the
    31    constructor's fit from the separated frame and tuple to the true ones
    32    (`trans`).  The only inclusion the induction itself produces is the
    33    separation `sep ⊆ carrier`.
    34  
    35  **What is used of a class** (charter items 2, 4): its clause at each
    36  frame the induction visits (`OkAt`: monotone in its own holes, a closed
    37  tuple, the fibre law) and ONE fact per class tying a frame to the true
    38  one, `trans`: a constructor fitting at an admissible frame, at holes
    39  below the true carrier, fits at the true frame and the true carrier.  At
    40  the term level `trans` is `LfpDatum.hfits_mono` along the relation
    41  between the instantiation's two hole frames (the constructor's
    42  positivity AT THE INSTANTIATION, `CtorPos` — what `nestPos`'s container
    43  descent certifies, keyed by the instantiation) followed by the clause's
    44  own `fitsMono` at the true frame.  Nothing is asked of a container "in
    45  its parameter": no monotonicity of its value or carrier, no Bekić, no
    46  joint (wide) operator.

== ConLeche/SetModel/NestRecCls.lean#L6-L29
     6  /-!
     7  # The nested kit's induction at the RECURSOR's classes
     8  
     9  The nested kit `NestKit` (`SetModel/NestRec.lean`: `trans` at every
    10  admissible frame) proves the induction principle of its majors,
    11  the tagged elements `nenc b m t x` of every CLAUSE class `b` (a member
    12  block, or a container at an instantiation — a positivity NODE),
    13  component `m`.  `NestNodeInd` is that principle, DECODED (a major's
    14  predecessors are the kit's `pred` at a decoding at the true frame and
    15  carrier), and the one interface the recursor side reads; `NestKit.toNodeInd`
    16  is its instance.
    17  
    18  The recursor model's graph kit (`graphKitG`,
    19  `Model/Inductives/BlockRecGraph.lean`) is stated over the RECURSOR's
    20  classes: recursor `c`'s majors are `tagged c t x`, its decodings are the
    21  rule data's, and its predecessors are the rule's call targets (`predR`).
    22  `NestNodeInd.ind_recNodesOn` transports the one to the other, with
    23  SEVERAL nodes per class (`Rel c b`: node `b` visits recursor `c`'s class
    24  at component `mOf c b`; one instantiation may be visited at several
    25  nodes), on a set `S` of classes that have nodes.
    26  The property is read back along every node of a class: `P'` holds at the
    27  node major `nenc b (mOf c b) t x` when `P` holds at `tagged c t x`
    28  for every related recursor `c`; the kit's predecessors must contain every
    29  related recursor's call targets (`hpredR`).

   879  spine with the rule's own (`BlockRuleDataAt`'s `mk` conjunct). -/
   880  theorem blockRecRuleLaw_gen {env : Env} {m₃ : EnvModel V env} {φ : Name → Nat}

== whitepaper/Fragment/EtaIota.lean#L402-L410
   402  /-- **The projection of the point is the point**, from the field's
   403  sort: if the projection's type, walked along the parameters, is
   404  `(x : D) → B` and `B` is a proposition at every member of `D` whenever
   405  `D` holds the point — the field's sort is at most the structure's, so

   407  projection at the point is the point.  This is what fails for an
   408  impredicative structure (a data field of a `Prop` structure), which

== whitepaper/Fragment/EtaIota.lean#L707-L724
   707  open EtaWit in
   708  /-- **Eta on the reduct of the major is outside the claims**.
   709  The major `maj := (fun x : A => g (k x)) a` is well-denoted
   710  and the point (a lambda that is the point constrains nothing, so `a` may
   711  lie outside `A`), and it β-reduces to `maj' := g (k a)`, which is not
   712  well-denoted (`k` is a graph over `A`).  The redex `rec minor maj` is
   713  well-denoted and not the point.  Eta-expanding the major's reduct,
   714  `minor (p0 maj')`, breaks the reduction claim; eta-expanding the major
   715  as it stands, `minor (p0 maj)`, satisfies it.  So the checker's eta
   716  path must not reduce the major first (lean4#15371 expands before the
   717  major's `whnf`). -/
   718  theorem etaIota_reduced_major_witness [LevelOracle] (φ : Name → Nat) (env : Env)
   719      (Γ : List Expr) :
   720      Red env Γ maj maj' ∧
   721      (∀ ρ : Nat → V, WellDenoted (witM (V := V)) φ ρ redex2 ∧ interp witM φ ρ redex2 ≠ pt ∧
   722        interp witM φ ρ maj = pt) ∧
   723      ¬ RedSem (EnvModel.empty (witM (V := V))) φ [] redex2 etaRed2 ∧
   724      RedSem (EnvModel.empty (witM (V := V))) φ [] redex2 eta2 := by

== whitepaper/Fragment/Decl.lean#L608-L618
   608  /-- **A theorem is accepted** (con-leche's theorem check): its
   609  statement `ci.type` and a proof `v` pass the definition check, and the
   610  statement is a proposition.  What is stored is the statement alone, as
   611  an assumption (`ConstKind.assumed`, `ci.kind`): a theorem never
   612  unfolds, in the checker (`Rules/Rel.lean`, only a definition unfolds)
   613  as in the fragment.  So two proofs of one statement store the same
   614  constant. -/
   615  def ThmOk (env : Env) (c : Name) (ci : ConstInfo) (v : Expr) : Prop :=
   616    ci.kind = .assumed ∧

   618    (∃ s u, Infer env [] ci.type s ∧ Red env [] s (.sort u) ∧ LevelOracle.eq u .zero = true)

== whitepaper/Fragment/ModularModel.lean#L59-L79
    59  /-- **A proof's set is the point**, at every list of levels: the value
