    61  theorem defVal_eq_pt {env : Env} (m : EnvModel V env) {c : Name} {ci : ConstInfo} {v : Expr}
    62      (hok : DefOk env c ci) (hk : ci.kind = .defn v)
    63      (hp : ∃ s u, Infer env [] ci.type s ∧ Red env [] s (.sort u) ∧ LevelOracle.eq u .zero = true)
    64      (ls : List Nat) : defVal m.M ci v ls = pt := by
    65    obtain ⟨-, ⟨s₀, u₀, hT, hsu⟩, ⟨v', T, hk', hv, hd, -⟩, -⟩ := hok
    66    rw [hk] at hk'; cases hk'
    67    obtain ⟨s, u, hs, hsr, hu⟩ := hp
    68    let φ := valOf ci.lparams ls
    69    have hvsem := infer_sound (m := m) (φ := φ) hv base (Sat_nil _ _ _)
    70    obtain ⟨hTw, hTmem⟩ := Infer.mem_typeU_of (m := m) (φ := φ)
    71      (infer_sound hT) (red_sound hsu) (Sat_nil _ _ base)
    72    have heq := defeq_sound (m := m) (φ := φ) hd base (Sat_nil _ _ _)
    73      hvsem.2.1 hTw hvsem.2.2.1.ne_pt (IsTy_of_mem_typeU hTmem).ne_pt
    74    obtain ⟨-, hU⟩ := Infer.mem_typeU_of (m := m) (φ := φ)
    75      (infer_sound hs) (red_sound hsr) (Sat_nil _ _ base)
    76    rw [eval_eq_of_oracle hu, Level.eval, mem_typeU_zero] at hU
    77    have hmem := hvsem.2.2.2
    78    rw [heq] at hmem
    79    exact eq_pt_of_mem_univ_zero hU hmem

== whitepaper/Fragment/ModularModel.lean#L157-L164
   157  /-- **A qualified name**: an ordinary constant is named by its home
   158  module and its name; a proof by its name and statement (two proofs of
   159  one statement are one constant: the model gives every proof the
   160  point). -/
   161  inductive Key where
   162    | qual (module : Nat) (n : Name)
   163    | proof (n : Name) (lparams : List Name) (type : Expr)
   164    deriving DecidableEq

== whitepaper/Fragment/ModularModel.lean#L166-L176
   166  /-- **A module**: its declarations; its **context**, the environment
   167  they are checked against; for each name of the context, the earlier
   168  module it is read from, its home (`src`); which of its own
   169  constants are proofs (`proofs`); and its **resolution** of names to
   170  qualified names (`res`). -/
   171  structure Module where
   172    decls : List Decl
   173    context : Env
   174    src : Name → Nat
   175    proofs : Name → Bool
   176    res : Name → Key

== whitepaper/Fragment/ModularModel.lean#L178-L179
   178  /-- **A module's own environment**: its context with its declarations. -/
   179  def Module.own (m : Module) : Env := applyAll m.decls m.context

== whitepaper/Fragment/ModularModel.lean#L185-L189
   185  /-- **The part of module `b`'s own environment that module `i` reads
   186  as `b` does**, for an environment `E` of `i`: the names `E` stores and
   187  `i` resolves as `b` resolves them. -/
   188  def readsAlike (dev : Nat → Module) (i : Nat) (E : Env) (b : Nat) : Env :=
   189    ⟨(dev b).own.consts.filter fun p => (E.find? p.1).isSome && (dev i).res p.1 == (dev b).res p.1⟩

== whitepaper/Fragment/ModularModel.lean#L206-L221
   206  /-- **An environment of module `i` reads from earlier modules**: every
   207  constant it stores is read from an earlier module, its home; it
   208  refines the home's own constant and lies within the part of the home's
   209  own environment `i` reads as the home does; `i` resolves it as the
   210  home does; and a type former stored as such comes with its
   211  constructors.  A type former may be read as an assumption of its type
   212  (it refines the type former), and then brings no constructors. -/
   213  structure ReadsFrom (dev : Nat → Module) (i : Nat) (E : Env) : Prop where
   214    src_lt : ∀ n, (E.find? n).isSome → (dev i).src n < i
   215    le : ∀ n ci, E.find? n = some ci →
   216      ∃ ci', (dev ((dev i).src n)).own.find? n = some ci' ∧ ci.Le ci' ∧
   217        EntryScoped (readsAlike dev i E ((dev i).src n)) E ci
   218    res : ∀ n, (E.find? n).isSome → (dev i).res n = (dev ((dev i).src n)).res n
   219    blocks : ∀ n ci nP nI cs S, E.find? n = some ci → ci.kind = .induct nP nI cs S →
   220      S.nest = none → E.find? S.name = some S.indInfo ∧
   221        ∀ (j : Nat) (c : CtorSpec), S.ctors[j]? = some c → E.find? c.name = some (S.ctorInfo c)

== whitepaper/Fragment/ModularModel.lean#L191-L204
   191  /-- **A constant within an environment**: what its laws read — its
   192  type, its value, its rules with their constructors, its block — is in
   193  scope there, and the constructors a recursor's rules name are stored
   194  there as in `E'`. -/
   195  def EntryScoped (C E' : Env) (ci : ConstInfo) : Prop :=
   196    Expr.Scoped C ci.lparams 0 ci.type ∧
   197    (∀ v, ci.value? = some v → Expr.Scoped C ci.lparams 0 v) ∧
   198    (∀ nP nM nMin nI rules, ci.kind = .recursor nP nM nMin nI rules → ∀ rl ∈ rules,
   199      Expr.Scoped C ci.lparams 0 rl.rhs ∧
   200      ∃ cij, C.find? rl.ctor = some cij ∧ E'.find? rl.ctor = some cij ∧
   201        Expr.Scoped C cij.lparams 0 cij.type) ∧
   202    (∀ nP nI cs S, ci.kind = .induct nP nI cs S → S.nest = none →
   203      S.Scoped C ∧ (C.find? S.name).isSome ∧
   204        ∀ (j : Nat) (c : CtorSpec), S.ctors[j]? = some c → (C.find? c.name).isSome)

== whitepaper/Fragment/ModularModel.lean#L223-L236
   223  /-- **The local checks at module `i`.**  They read the module and the
   224  earlier modules its context draws from — their own environments and
   225  resolutions — and nothing else:
   226  
   227  * the context reads from earlier modules (`ReadsFrom`);
   228  * the declarations are accepted against the context, and a constant
   229    flagged a proof is a declaration of a proposition;
   230  * an own name resolves to its own qualified name. -/

   234    flags : FlagsOk (dev i).proofs (dev i).context (dev i).decls

== whitepaper/Fragment/ModularModel.lean#L243-L244

== whitepaper/Fragment/ModularModel.lean#L565-L577
   565  /-- **Modular checking** (the theorem): if every module up to `i`
   566  passes its local checks, there is one assignment of sets to the
   567  qualified names — every proof the point — under which every module's
   568  own environment, read through its resolution, has a model. -/
   569  theorem modular (dev : Nat → Module) :
   570      ∀ i, (∀ j ≤ i, Valid dev j) →
   571        ∃ G : Key → List Nat → V, (∀ n lps T ls, G (.proof n lps T) ls = pt) ∧
   572          ∀ j ≤ i, ∃ m : BlockModel V (dev j).own,
   573            ∀ n, ((dev j).own.find? n).isSome → ∀ ls, m.M n ls = resAssign G (dev j) n ls
   574    | 0, hall => modular_step dev 0 hall (fun _ _ => pt) (fun _ _ _ _ => rfl) (fun _ hj => absurd hj (Nat.not_lt_zero _))
   575    | i + 1, hall => by
   576      obtain ⟨G₀, hpt, hprev⟩ := modular dev i fun j hj => hall j (Nat.le_succ_of_le hj)
   577      exact modular_step dev (i + 1) hall G₀ hpt fun j hj => hprev j (Nat.le_of_lt_succ hj)

== whitepaper/Fragment/ModularModel.lean#L580-L585
   580  /-- **Every module's own environment has a model.** -/
   581  theorem modular_model (dev : Nat → Module) (i : Nat) (h : ∀ j ≤ i, Valid dev j) :
   582      Nonempty (BlockModel V (dev i).own) := by
   583    obtain ⟨G, -, hall⟩ := modular V dev i h
   584    obtain ⟨m, -⟩ := hall i (Nat.le_refl i)
   585    exact ⟨m⟩

   600  /-- **Every statement a module stores holds in its model** — in
   601  particular every assumption of a compared module (a hole): its type,
   602  at every instantiation, has a member. -/

== ConLeche/Rules/Rel.lean#L307-L332
   307    /-- **The `And` rescue** (`majorToCtor`'s `And` branch,
   308    `Kernel/Core.lean`; `And` only, by ruling): `And.intro a b
   309    (.proj And 0 h) (.proj And 1 h)` is fabricated for a stuck proof
   310    `h`, certified the K branch's way; the last four premises are the
   311    major's half of the `proofIrrel` run, as in the K branch. -/
   312    | rescueAnd {d : Nat} {major tm tmaj fab tf tp ttp : Expr} {v : Level} {recName : Name}
   313        {cv : ConstantVal} {mI rP : Nat} {rl : RecRule} {cvj : ConstantVal}
   314        {cnP cnF : Nat} {tus ust : List Level} {cvT : ConstantVal}
   315        {caps : IndCaps} :
   316        env.find? recName = some (.recInfo cv mI rP [rl]) →
   317        env.find? rl.ctor = some (.ctorInfo cvj cnP cnF) →
   318        (cvj.type.piResult).getAppFn = .const andName tus →
   319        env.find? andName = some (.indInfo cvT caps) →
   320        Infer env .io d major tm → Red env d tm tmaj →
   321        tmaj.getAppFn = .const andName ust →
   322        tmaj.getAppArgs.length = cnP →
   323        cvj.levelParams.length = ust.length →
   324        andRescueSlots env rl.ctor cnP ust = true →
   325        fab = Expr.mkAppN (.const rl.ctor ust)
   326          (tmaj.getAppArgs ++ [.proj andName 0 major, .proj andName 1 major]) →
   327        fab.wscopedB d = true → fab.looseBVarsBounded 0 = true →
   328        fab.fvarLeaves.all (fun l => major.fvarLeaves.contains l) = true →
   329        Infer env .io d fab tf → DefEq env d tmaj tf →
   330        Infer env .io d major tp → Infer env .io d tp ttp →
   331        Red env d ttp (.sort v) → Level.isEquiv v .zero = some true →
   332        Red env d major fab

== ConLeche/Cached/Installed.lean#L441-L446
   441  def checkDecls (mode : CheckMode) (pins : List NatOpPinSet)
   442      (ds : Array Declaration) :
   443      Except (CheckError × Nat) Env := do
   444    let p ← ds.foldlM (installDeclStep mode pins) (0, mkFEnv Env.empty, #[])
   445    checkPendingList mode p.2.1 p.2.2.toList
   446    pure p.2.1.env

== ConLeche/Cached/Installed.lean#L341-L352
   341  The driver's check phase — the in-thread loop or a pool of workers —
   342  runs `checkRecord` on every record.  Its result is the record's own
   343  evidence: on an accept the `GroupChecked` fact of that record, on a
   344  failure the error tagged with the record's fold position, the tag
   345  `checkPendingList` gives.  A worker hands back exactly this (a `Nat`
   346  and an erased proof, or the error), so the thread that computed a
   347  check is irrelevant to what it proves, and the results of any number
   348  of workers, in whatever order they finished, are assembled into
   349  `∀ i, GroupChecked mode e i` by `collectChecks` — a walk over the
   350  results in record order, which is also what makes the verdict of a
   351  pool the verdict of the walk `checkPendingList`: the first failing
   352  record in fold order.  Nothing here is `IO`. -/

== ConLeche/Term/Syntax.lean#L188-L219
   188  inductive Term where
   189    /-- de Bruijn index -/
   190    | bvar (i : Nat)
   191    /-- `Sort u` at a concrete level -/
   192    | sort (u : Nat)
   193    /-- a built-in constant at a concrete level instantiation -/
   194    | const (c : BConst) (us : List Nat)
   195    /-- application -/
   196    | app (f a : Term)
   197    /-- `fun (_ : ty) => body` -/
   198    | lam (ty body : Term)
   199    /-- `(_ : ty) → body` -/
   200    | pi (ty body : Term)
   201    /-- `let _ := val; body`, **without the type**: the body is under one
   202    binder, read at the value -/
   203    | letE (val body : Term)
   204    /-- `@Eq _ lhs rhs`, **without the type**: the interpretation is
   205    `⟦eqE a b⟧ = eqv ⟦a⟧ ⟦b⟧`, so soundness never constrains the type,
   206    and no definition and no theorem in any tier reads the type, so
   207    the constructor does not carry it; a producer that knows the type
   208    simply drops it. -/
   209    | eqE (lhs rhs : Term)
   210    /-- First field of a pair.  Carries **only** the subject: the pair's
   211    type arguments come from the typing premise `Γ ⊢ p : Σ A B`,
   212    not from the term — see the module docstring.  Interpreted by
   213    `sfst`, i.e. literally `interp`'s clause. -/
   214    | fst (e : Term)
   215    /-- Second field of a pair; the `fst` twin, interpreted by `ssnd`. -/
   216    | snd (e : Term)
   217    /-- the canonical (irrelevant) proof of a derivable equation -/
   218    | prf
   219    deriving Repr, Inhabited

== ConLeche/Verify/Denote.lean#L153-L154
   153  @[expose] def denote (cval : Name → (Name → Nat) → Term) (env : Env)
   154      (φ : Name → Nat) : (d : Nat) → Expr → Option Term

== ConLeche/Semantics/Interp.lean#L134-L145
   134  noncomputable def interp : (Nat → V) → Term → V
   135    | ρ, .bvar i => ρ i
   136    | _, .sort u => univ u
   137    | _, .const c us => bval V c us
   138    | ρ, .app f a => SetTheory.app (interp ρ f) (interp ρ a)
   139    | ρ, .lam A b => lamV (interp ρ A) fun x => interp (cons x ρ) b
   140    | ρ, .pi A B => piV (interp ρ A) fun x => interp (cons x ρ) B
   141    | ρ, .letE v b => interp (cons (interp ρ v) ρ) b
   142    | ρ, .eqE a b => eqv (interp ρ a) (interp ρ b)
   143    | ρ, .fst e => sfst (interp ρ e)
   144    | ρ, .snd e => ssnd (interp ρ e)
   145    | _, .prf => pt

== ConLeche/Rules/Rel.lean#L640-L649
   640  /-- **The full-grade telescope certificate** (`iotaCertsFull`,
   641  `Kernel/Core.lean`; ι's case 3, task #342 L10): each argument's
   642  FULL-grade type is definitionally equal to its binder domain, the
   643  domains instantiated along the spine; no slot is skipped. -/
   644  inductive CertsF (env : Env) : Nat → Expr → List Expr → Prop where
   645    | nil {d : Nat} {T : Expr} : CertsF env d T []
   646    | cert {d : Nat} {ty body arg ta : Expr} {rest : List Expr} :
   647        Infer env .full d arg ta → DefEq env d ta ty →
   648        CertsF env d (body.instantiate1 arg) rest →
   649        CertsF env d (.forallE ty body) (arg :: rest)

== ConLeche/Rules/Rel.lean#L651-L656
   651  /-- **Pairwise definitional equality** (`defEqList`, `Kernel/Core.lean`). -/
   652  inductive DefEqList (env : Env) : Nat → List Expr → List Expr → Prop where
   653    | nil {d : Nat} : DefEqList env d [] []
   654    | cons {d : Nat} {a b : Expr} {as bs : List Expr} :
   655        DefEq env d a b → DefEqList env d as bs →
   656        DefEqList env d (a :: as) (b :: bs)

== ConLeche/Rules/Rel.lean#L508-L547
   508  /-- **λ-telescope congruence, typed at the innermost level only**
   509  (task #349; the fragment's `DefEqLams`).  Two λ-telescopes are compared
   510  level by level: the domains at every level, the opened bodies' FULL-grade
   511  types only where the comparison stops descending through two λs — where
   512  the checker's `Expr.lamPair?` fails (`defeqLams`, `Kernel/Core.lean`).
   513  
   514  *Why the outer levels need no type comparison.*  The type comparison is
   515  what makes λ-congruence's claim **unconditional** — `DefEq`'s claim says
   516  nothing where a side is the point, and two bodies in one type are both
   517  the point or neither — and an unconditional equality of the bodies at
   518  every value of the variable is an equality of the λs, with no type at
   519  all; so the claim propagates outward through any number of levels.
   520  
   521  *Unequal depth, and reduction between levels.*  The descent continues
   522  only through two **syntactic** λs (`outer`'s premise is this relation
   523  itself, which has no reduction rule).  Where one body is not a λ — the
   524  comparison ends in η or any other rule, possibly after δ or whnf steps —
   525  that level is the innermost one (`inner`), and its bodies' types are
   526  inferred and compared at the full grade.  Syntactically equal λs
   527  (`refl`) are equal outright. -/
   528  inductive DefEqLams (env : Env) : Nat → Expr → Expr → Prop where
   529    /-- Syntactically equal sides (the checker's `a == b` fast path). -/
   530    | refl {d : Nat} {a : Expr} : DefEqLams env d a a
   531    /-- The innermost level: domains, bodies opened with the RIGHT
   532    domain, and the opened bodies' full-grade types. -/
   533    | inner {d : Nat} {ty₁ body₁ ty₂ body₂ t₁ t₂ : Expr} :
   534        DefEq env d ty₁ ty₂ →
   535        DefEq env (d + 1) (body₁.instantiate1 (.fvar d ty₂))
   536          (body₂.instantiate1 (.fvar d ty₂)) →
   537        Infer env .full (d + 1) (body₁.instantiate1 (.fvar d ty₂)) t₁ →
   538        Infer env .full (d + 1) (body₂.instantiate1 (.fvar d ty₂)) t₂ →
   539        DefEq env (d + 1) t₁ t₂ →
   540        DefEqLams env d (.lam ty₁ body₁) (.lam ty₂ body₂)
   541    /-- An outer level: the domains, and the opened bodies by this
   542    relation — no inference, no type comparison. -/
   543    | outer {d : Nat} {ty₁ body₁ ty₂ body₂ : Expr} :
   544        DefEq env d ty₁ ty₂ →
   545        DefEqLams env (d + 1) (body₁.instantiate1 (.fvar d ty₂))
   546          (body₂.instantiate1 (.fvar d ty₂)) →
   547        DefEqLams env d (.lam ty₁ body₁) (.lam ty₂ body₂)

== ConLeche/Denotes.lean#L121-L124
   121  /-- `Denotes cval env φ ρ e v`: the term `e` denotes the set `v`.  See
   122  the module docstring. -/

   124      (BVarIdx → V) → Expr → V → Prop

== ConLeche/Denotes.lean#L248-L268
   248  structure Model (V : Type w) [SetTheory V] (env : Env) where
   249    /-- the set a constant denotes, per level assignment -/
   250    cval : Name → (LevelParam → Nat) → V
   251    /-- every stored constant is a member of what its type denotes, at
   252    every level assignment (and every variable environment — the type
   253    is closed) -/
   254    mem : ∀ c ∈ env.consts, ∀ (φ : LevelParam → Nat) (ρ : BVarIdx → V),
   255      ∃ T, Denotes cval env φ ρ c.toConstantVal.type T ∧ cval c.name φ ∈ˢ T
   256    /-- whatever the built-in `False` denotes is the empty set -/
   257    false_empty : ∀ (φ : LevelParam → Nat) (ρ : BVarIdx → V) (F : V),
   258      Denotes cval env φ ρ (.const falseName []) F → F = empty
   259    /-- whatever the built-in `Eq` denotes is set equality: at a type `A`
   260    of the universe the level `u` names, and two of its members `a` and
   261    `b`, `@Eq.{u} A a b` denotes the truth value of `a = b`.  The three
   262    membership premises are the graph's domains — `Eq`'s denotation is a
   263    three-fold graph over `univ (Level.eval φ u)`, then over `A`, then
   264    over `A` again, and a graph read off its domain says nothing -/
   265    eq_equality : ∀ (u : Level) (φ : LevelParam → Nat) (ρ : BVarIdx → V) (E A a b : V),
   266      Denotes cval env φ ρ (.const eqName [u]) E →
   267      A ∈ˢ univ (Level.eval φ u) → a ∈ˢ A → b ∈ˢ A →
   268      app (app (app E A) a) b = eqv a b

   197        ∀ ρ : Nat → V,
